regions.name: Dewleaf Town
regions.description: Tall grass, bugs and friendly first finds.

gym.title: Dewleaf Town Gym Leader
gym.intro: So you're the one catching everything on my island! Let's see if your team glows as bright as my bugs.
gym.lose: Whoa, that was bright! Take the Glow Badge. You've earned it.
gym.win: The glow fades… train up and come back!

regions.name: Sunny Shore
regions.description: Palms, warm sand and Water types.

gym.title: Sunny Shore Gym Leader
gym.intro: Ahahaha, welcome to the shore! Let me show you the elegance of water Pokémon, in perfect harmony with their trainer.
gym.lose: Splendid! A performance worthy of the Tide Badge. Please, accept it.
gym.win: Ahaha… the tide was not with you today.

regions.name: Ashen Peak
regions.description: Volcanic ash, lava and Fire types.

gym.title: Ashen Peak Gym Leader
gym.intro: Welcome to the volcano! My fire Pokémon will scorch you with heat that burns hotter than the lava. Let's go!
gym.lose: Oh… I guess I was trying too hard. You've earned the Ember Badge!
gym.win: Hah! Too hot for you? Cool off and try again!

regions.name: Misty Pyre
regions.description: Graves, incense and things that go bump.

gym.title: Misty Pyre Gym Leader
gym.intro: Ahahaha! I trained on this mountain, where the spirits rest. My ghosts and I share a bond you can't see. Can you beat us?
gym.lose: Oh, darn. I've gone and lost. Take the Spirit Badge… the ghosts approve of you.
gym.win: Ahahaha! The spirits win again. Come back when you can see them!

regions.name: Frostveil Peak
regions.description: Deep snow, frozen ponds and Ice types.

gym.title: Frostveil Peak Gym Leader
gym.intro: Welcome to the summit. I came all this way for a trainer worth freezing… Show me your heat, if you have any.
gym.lose: What fiery passion… Take the Frost Badge. The peak has never felt so warm.
gym.win: Too cold for you? The peak is not for the faint of heart.

regions.name: Skyhigh Cliffs
regions.description: Blossom cliffs above the clouds, and Flying types.

gym.title: Skyhigh Cliffs Gym Leader
gym.intro: I have become one with the bird Pokémon and soared the skies above these cliffs. Can you keep up with us?
gym.lose: Never before have I seen a trainer fly so high. Take the Feather Badge.
gym.win: Grounded! Come back when your team can ride the wind.

regions.name: Voltage Works
regions.description: Pylons, scrap and crackling Electric and Steel types.

gym.title: Voltage Works Gym Leader
gym.intro: Wahahahah! Fine, I lost my job running the works, but I'll never lose a battle! Get ready to be shocked!
gym.lose: Wahahahah! Fine, I lost! You electrified me! Take the Dynamo Badge!
gym.win: Wahahahah! Shocking, isn't it? Recharge and come back!

regions.name: Dragonspire
regions.description: The last climb: crimson peaks where Dragons nest.

gym.title: Dragonspire Gym Leader
gym.intro: I am the last Gym of the isles. To battle Dragons, a trainer needs the one thing that matters most… Do you have it?
gym.lose: Superb! You've earned the Legend Badge. Every island is yours… for now.
gym.win: You lack what it takes. Come back when you have it!

bountyRules: A shared board of four jobs changes every three days.
At least one job on each board has no badge requirement.
Meet a job’s badge requirement before its progress counts.
Claim completed jobs in Events → Bounties for tickets. Some jobs also bring a costume encounter onto your route.
evolutionRules: Friendship evolutions can happen at Good Buddy (6 hearts), or at level 20. Gender, time, and move requirements still apply. Eevee’s Espeon and Umbreon paths remain a player choice.
Normal level evolutions happen when their requirements are met. Branching species let you choose an evolution in the PC.
Shiny, Void, Prismatic, and Perfect Pokémon wait for you to evolve them from the PC.
Everstone stops automatic level evolution and automatic evolution on receiving a trade. Remove it to let level evolution proceed.
Trade evolutions can use a Linking Cord instead of another player. No held evolution item is required.
Eevee can become Espeon or Umbreon from level 20 by your choice, regardless of the clock. Sylveon also requires a Fairy-type move. Leafeon uses a Leaf Stone; Glaceon uses an Ice Stone.
Regional forms listed as wild forms are caught separately rather than evolved from their standard form.
Day is 6 am–7 pm and night is 7 pm–6 am, using your device clock.
Costumes without an evolved costume stay in their current form.
Tower teammates follow the Tower's separate evolution rules.

guides.summary: Build a party, set your catch rules and work toward the first Gym badge.

sections.heading: Returning player? Load your account save first
paragraphs: If you already play on another device, sign in with the same Discord account and review the account-save offer before creating a new starter. Cloud saves are supported from 0.56.0.

sections.heading: Your first hunt
paragraphs: Begin in Dewleaf Town with a level 7 starter, $300, 20 Poké Balls, 5 Great Balls and 3 Potions. Your party automatically fights wild Pokémon. Catch rules decide which encounters receive balls instead.

sections.heading: A useful first route
bullets: Open Catch and enable New species to fill your Pokédex. Keep Shiny, Void, Prismatic and Perfect catches enabled if you want rare finds.
Use Party & PC to add catches to your team and compare their stats.
Defeat six bosses on Dewleaf Town, then challenge Matt from Islands. Winning the Glow Badge opens Sunny Shore.
Claim completed Field Research and achievement rewards. Buy balls and upgrades at the Mart.

sections.heading: Playing on iPhone or Android (0.57.0)
paragraphs: The official browser game now has a phone layout and touch controls. Open play.playtallgrass.com and use your Discord account to continue the same cloud save. See Playing on a phone for installation, login codes and touch navigation.

guides.title: Islands, Gyms and badges
guides.summary: Eight islands form the main progression route. Each Gym badge opens the next island.

sections.heading: Progression table
paragraphs: Boss requirements are per island. The wild level ranges below describe the ordinary island bands; individual encounters can vary. Each Gym has four Pokémon, with the listed ace at the highest level.

sections.heading: How to challenge a Gym
paragraphs: Open Islands, select the island and complete its boss requirement. Press Challenge when the Gym opens. Your party fights the Gym automatically. If a fight is already running, the challenge can be queued.

sections.heading: First wins and rematch rewards
paragraphs: Your first Gym win awards the badge item in the table, three Rare Candies, five Ultra Balls, one Max Potion, two Revives and a random held item other than Everstone. First-win money is $1,500 multiplied by the island’s position: $1,500 at Dewleaf Town through $12,000 at Dragonspire.
Rematch wins award one Rare Candy, two Super Potions and $600 multiplied by island position. When the island’s total Gym wins reach a multiple of three, a rematch also awards a Master Ball.

sections.heading: Travel and rematches
paragraphs: Select an open island and use Fly here. Travel waits for the current fight to finish. Gym rematch wins make that island’s wild Pokémon stronger.

sections.heading: Received Pokémon and level caps
paragraphs: Pokémon received above your badge-based level cap temporarily fight at the capped level. Their original level is remembered, and winning more badges restores that strength.

sections.heading: Boss counter and completed Pokédex (0.54.3)
paragraphs: The next-boss counter is shown on the island Pokédex chip and in Islands. Once that island's Pokédex is complete, its boss interval is 20 encounters instead of 35.

guides.title: Island checklists
guides.summary: Complete an island’s non-legendary Pokédex checklist for a one-time prize.

sections.heading: What counts
paragraphs: Open Islands and check Island checklist. Catch every non-legendary species assigned to that island, then press Claim. Species remain registered after you evolve, trade or transfer their Pokémon.

sections.heading: Completion rewards
paragraphs: Every completed island awards a Master Ball, 10 Rare Candies and a Big Nugget. Money rises by $5,000 for each island in the route.

guides.title: Trainer ranks
guides.summary: Register different species to raise your rank, improve wild encounter variety and unlock stronger balls at the Mart.

sections.heading: Key unlocks
bullets: Youngster: rare Pokémon begin appearing.
Bug Catcher: Great Balls become available at the Mart.
Ace Trainer: Ultra Balls become available. Legendary roaming also depends on Gym progress.
Later ranks improve rare-look odds and the mix of wild encounter rarities.

sections.heading: Ranks and badges
paragraphs: Rank comes from registered species. Badges come from Gym victories. They are separate goals, so a high rank does not automatically open later islands or Events.

guides.title: Legendary and Mythical Pokémon
guides.summary: Wake an island’s roaming legends with badges, and look to Raids for Mythicals.

sections.heading: Waking legends
paragraphs: An island’s roaming Legendary Pokémon awaken after you have beaten its Gym and earned at least three badges in total. Islands shows which legends are asleep and what you still need. Mythicals are excluded from ordinary wild island encounters.

sections.heading: Hunting a known legend
paragraphs: The Poké Radar can target a Legendary only after it is registered and its island’s legends are awake. Mythicals cannot be Radar targets.

sections.heading: Receiving rare Pokémon
paragraphs: Receiving Legendary, Mythical, Void or Prismatic Pokémon through player trading or the Night Market requires five badges, alongside the other trade and island restrictions.

sections.heading: Mythical and Ultra Beast labels (0.57.3)
paragraphs: Cards, hunt call-outs, battles, Raids, trades, the Night Market and away summaries now use the correct Mythical or Ultra Beast name and mark. The update changes presentation, rather than the underlying rarity rules. Searching legendary still finds them alongside ordinary Legendaries.

guides.title: Events menu
guides.summary: Events brings together rotating hunts, challenges, collection rewards and player trading.

rows: Hunt featured Pokémon with boosted rare-look odds.
Fight bosses with other trainers and collect Raid Eggs.
Build a squad for a climb and choose rewards between floors.
Complete rotating jobs for Bounty Tickets and costume encounters.
Fill your rare-look collection book and open prize balls.
Exchange a spare Pokémon for a surprise.
Buy and sell rare Pokémon for Glimmer.
Convert Rare Candy into family Candy and hatch ready eggs together.
Open capsules, play Slots and spend Coins at the Prize Counter.

sections.heading: Unlocks
paragraphs: Locked activities show the badge requirement in their own tab. Wonder Trade opens at two badges; Outbreaks and Night Market at three; Raids at five.

sections.heading: Limited-time events
paragraphs: A live event banner appears above the game with its remaining time. Events can boost Shiny odds, EXP or money, add an event outbreak or run a Raid Hour with bonus eggs. Event outbreaks are listed for trainers who have reached the featured island.

sections.heading: Trainer gifts (0.54.4)
paragraphs: Pokémon received as gifts from the Tallgrass team have an E tag beside their name.

sections.heading: Live surprise events (0.57.4)
paragraphs: Watch for Golden Hour bonuses to Shiny odds, EXP and money; Spotlight outbreaks of one Pokémon on every island; route-wide weather; Glo messages; Candy Rain; and Mystery Egg drops. The team starts these live. Check the banner for actual bonuses and remaining time.

sections.heading: Hatch Rush (0.57.5)
paragraphs: A golden egg banner announces a live 2× or 3× boost to Day Care egg production and hatch speed. Per-egg odds stay unchanged.

guides.title: Mass Outbreaks
guides.summary: Featured Pokémon appear more often on selected islands; the current look multiplier is ×1.

sections.heading: Where and when
paragraphs: Open Events → Outbreaks to see the current islands, featured Pokémon, remaining time and upcoming outbreaks. The list refreshes every six hours and is shared between trainers. Fly there starts travel to the featured island.

sections.heading: Encounter bonuses
paragraphs: When a Radar target is not selected, an active outbreak has a 12% chance to replace the ordinary wild encounter, approximately one in eight. This improves access to the featured species. The 0.57.3 look multiplier is ×1.

sections.heading: Current rare-look odds: ×1
paragraphs: The actual featured outbreak uses the ordinary rank and Charm chances in 0.57.3, with no additional outbreak look multiplier. At Rookie rank without Charm, Shiny remains 1 in 2,400. Radar is a different encounter path and can still boost its own target odds.
During the season, Spectral derives from the applicable Prismatic base. Live odds events are separate; check the in-game odds display for active server bonuses.

sections.heading: Special visitors
paragraphs: The outbreak page can show a visiting costume Pokémon and a schedule of upcoming featured hunts. Check this page before choosing an island.

sections.heading: Team-run event outbreaks
paragraphs: Limited-time event outbreaks can appear alongside the normal rotating list. Trainers who can reach the selected island can see them. Check the event banner and countdown for the active bonus and duration.

sections.heading: Looks label and phone navigation (0.57.0)
paragraphs: The older outbreak Looks ×3 label refers to Shiny, Void and Prismatic odds. It does not multiply the separate Perfect-IV roll or stack with a successful Radar selection. On a phone, open Events from the bottom navigation to reach outbreaks.

sections.heading: Current 0.57.3 multiplier
paragraphs: The installed 0.57.3 build uses Looks ×1 for outbreak replacements: no extra Shiny, Void, Prismatic or Spectral chance multiplier from the outbreak itself. The species targeting still applies. This replaces the ×3 described for older versions; Radar remains a separate path.

sections.heading: Spotlight outbreaks (0.57.4)
paragraphs: A team-run Spotlight event features outbreaks of one Pokémon on every island. Open Events → Outbreaks and check the event countdown. Live event values are separate from ordinary outbreak tuning.

guides.title: Bounty board
guides.summary: Four rotating jobs reward Bounty Tickets, with costume encounters attached to selected bounties.

sections.heading: Rotation and claiming
paragraphs: The board refreshes every three days. Only jobs you have unlocked can progress. Finish a job and press Claim before the board changes. A costume reward queues that Pokémon to appear on your route next; it does not place the Pokémon directly in your PC.

rows: Catch 2 Shiny Pokémon of the chosen type
Defeat 4 bosses with the chosen trait
Catch a Shiny, Void or Prismatic outbreak Pokémon
Reach the chosen Tower floor: 20, 30 or 40
Clear a raid as top damage dealer with a friend in it

sections.heading: Alpha boss recruitment (0.54.5)
paragraphs: Alpha boss notices explain that defeating the boss can recruit it. Alpha bosses cannot be caught with Poké Balls.

guides.title: Stamp Book
guides.summary: Collect stamps for species you have owned in Shiny, Void, Prismatic and Perfect looks, plus costume looks.

sections.heading: Using the book
paragraphs: Open Events → Stamps. Choose a rare-look collection and an island or Legends page. Browse the pages, search for a Pokémon and open earned prize balls. Open all collects every waiting book reward together.

sections.heading: What the rewards contain
paragraphs: Early island milestones award money, Bounty Tickets and balls or Rare Candy. A completed island look-page awards a Master Ball, two Big Nuggets, a costume reward, money and tickets. Exact money and ticket rewards rise with the island and collection.

sections.heading: Costume collection
paragraphs: Costume-stamp milestones begin at 3, 10, 25 and 50. Owning every costume in every available look has its own final prize.

sections.heading: Spooky 2026 challenge page
paragraphs: Six seasonal challenges: find your first Spectral; find 3; find a Spectral Ghost-type; find a Spectral Legendary or Mythical; hatch one from a Day Care egg; and find 25 Spectrals (Spirit Collector; reduced from 50 in 0.57.4). Earlier self-found Spectrals count, but trades do not. Complete the page before the season ends for the Spooky 2026 card frame and title. These challenges never add to normal book totals.

sections.heading: Spirit Collector update (0.57.4)
paragraphs: Spirit Collector requires 25 self-found Spectrals. If you already have 25, the stamp completes automatically. Trading does not count toward the seasonal page.

guides.title: Wonder Trade
guides.summary: Send an eligible Pokémon for a surprise, with more daily trades as you earn badges.

sections.heading: Requirements
paragraphs: Wonder Trade opens with your second Gym badge and requires an online connection. Your daily allowance is five plus one for each Gym badge: seven at unlock, rising to thirteen with eight badges. Received Pokémon come from islands you have reached.

sections.heading: Choosing a Pokémon
paragraphs: Wonder Trade accepts eligible Pokémon even if they are your only or best copy of that species. Sending your only one prompts for confirmation. Favorites cannot be Wonder Traded until you remove their star. Party members, Day Care Pokémon, Founder Pokémon, fusions, Pokémon holding a Mega item and unopened hatch reveals remain ineligible.

sections.heading: Trading cooldown and items
paragraphs: A Pokémon received in a trade waits 14 days after arrival before it can be traded again. Check its card for the remaining time. The game may also block Pokémon it cannot validate. Held items are returned to your bag when a Wonder Trade succeeds.

sections.heading: If there is no suitable match
paragraphs: Your Pokémon can enter the Wonder Trade pool and wait for another trainer. The trade counts toward your daily allowance, and a Pokémon comes back to your PC when a suitable exchange becomes available. The game displays a note when it arrives. A failed exchange returns your Pokémon; a waiting exchange is a successful submission, so it does not return the original immediately.

sections.heading: Day Care babies (0.57.0)
paragraphs: The update fixes Day Care babies being rejected by Wonder Trade. Ordinary Wonder Trade requirements and protected-Pokémon restrictions still apply.

guides.title: Night Market
guides.summary: Browse and sell rare Pokémon using Glimmer, a separate market currency.

sections.heading: Opening the market
paragraphs: The Night Market opens with your third Gym badge and requires an online connection. Open Events → Night Market.

sections.heading: The four areas
bullets: Stalls: browse rare finds, search by species and filter by rare look, Perfect IVs or Legendary/Mythical status. Sort by newest, rarest or price.
My stall: choose a rare Pokémon, set its price and review the listing fee and duration before listing. It leaves your PC while listed. Take it down to return it.
Glimmer Shop: buy exclusive cosmetics, Spotlights, stall awnings and other market rewards.
Record board: see the market’s biggest sales.

sections.heading: What can be listed
paragraphs: Shiny, Void, Prismatic, Perfect and Alpha Pokémon qualify, as do Legendary and Mythical Pokémon. Held items stay in your bag. Purchased Pokémon can be sold again. The purchase screen checks island and badge restrictions before buying.

sections.heading: Earning Glimmer
paragraphs: Each eligible find pays once: Shiny adds 10 Glimmer, Void adds 30, Prismatic adds 80, Perfect adds 10 and Alpha adds 10. These bonuses add together; Legendary and Mythical finds multiply the result by three.

sections.heading: Check the listing before confirming
paragraphs: The My stall panel displays the current listing fee, listing limit and duration. Review these values and the Pokémon’s details before confirming a sale.

sections.heading: Editing a listed price
paragraphs: On My stall, press the price-edit pencil on your listing. Enter a valid Glimmer price and press the check mark, or press Enter. Escape cancels. The listing stays active and keeps its existing time remaining; changing the price does not restart the listing duration.

sections.heading: New seller eligibility notice (0.54.5)
paragraphs: If your account is too new to sell, the Night Market tells you how long remains before selling unlocks.

sections.heading: Online catch and Day Care sale fixes (0.57.0)
paragraphs: The release fixes sale-eligibility problems for Pokémon caught online and babies from Day Care. Market unlocks and other listing restrictions still apply. On a phone the market opens full screen with a close button.

sections.heading: Spectral and rarity labels
paragraphs: Spectrals qualify for listings and add 50 Glimmer to the look value. Mythical and Ultra Beast labels now distinguish them from Legendary on cards, searches and listings; the category naming change does not itself change rarity power or eligibility.

sections.heading: Minimum listing prices (0.57.5)
paragraphs: The price picker begins at the current minimum and displays it. Perfect, Alpha and Legendary status can raise the minimum; combinations use the applicable higher price rather than simply adding the base values.

Examples from this release: Shiny Alpha 300, Prismatic Alpha 2,250 and Void Legendary 800 Glimmer. Earlier evolution stages add 10% for the first stage and 5% for the middle stage of a three-stage line, or 5% for the first stage of a two-stage line. A Shiny Charmander therefore starts at 110 Glimmer. Check the picker for the exact combined minimum.

rows: Legendary or Mythical without a special look

sections.heading: Buying gates and Spectral limit (0.57.5)
paragraphs: Shiny purchases unlock from island 5, Void from island 7, and Prismatic and Spectral after every island is complete. Locked stalls show the required island. The market itself still opens with the third Gym badge.

Each player may make one Spectral listing per UTC day, resetting at midnight UTC. Listings below the new minimum prices returned to their sellers’ PCs with a Hunt log note; they can be listed again at a valid price.
Only N in the world now counts Spectral-only looks too and refreshes every few minutes. The minimum listing price is different from the Glimmer reward for finding a Pokémon.

guides.title: Professor’s Lab
guides.summary: Turn Rare Candy into family Candy, or open all ready eggs at once.

sections.heading: Family Candy conversion
paragraphs: Open Events → Lab and choose a family you currently own. Each Rare Candy becomes three family Candy, or one family Candy for a Legendary family. Select a quantity with −, + or All and confirm the conversion.

sections.heading: Choosing between levels and power-ups
paragraphs: Rare Candy can raise a Pokémon by one level from the PC. Converting it in the Lab spends that same Rare Candy to produce family Candy for power-ups. Pick the use that helps your team most.

sections.heading: Open all eggs
paragraphs: The Lab opens every ready egg in your basket in one quick reveal, including Raid and Costume eggs. Eggs that are still developing must become ready first.

guides.title: Style and cosmetics
guides.summary: Dress your trainer and customize your card, PC, ball effects and Shelf.

sections.heading: Cosmetic categories
bullets: Outfits change your trainer.
Themes recolor the interface.
Card frames and backgrounds decorate your trainer card and profile.
PC wallpapers are chosen per box.
Ball effects decorate throws, impacts, wobbles and catches.
Dolls and decor go on your Shelf.

sections.heading: Shopping
paragraphs: Open Events → Style to preview items and equip owned cosmetics. The three daily deals discount selected unowned ticket-priced items by 30%. Some items cost money, while others are rewards, capsule exclusives or Glimmer Shop exclusives.

sections.heading: The Shelf
paragraphs: Place up to six owned dolls or decor pieces on the Shelf beneath your trainer card. Friends see this display on your profile. Toggling a doll adds or removes it; adding beyond six replaces the oldest displayed piece.

sections.heading: Ball effects and performance
paragraphs: Cosmetics are for appearance. A ball effect does not turn the thrown ball into a different ball or change its catching strength.

sections.heading: Pokédex and Game Boy themes (0.57.5)
paragraphs: The Pokédex theme uses a black shell, gold crowns and trim, a blue lens and three lights. The active tab has a crown. Both it and Game Boy now style window frames, title bars, tabs and the strip bar.

Game Boy keeps its four-green palette for scenery and interface, while Pokémon retain their real colours so rare looks remain distinguishable. Text is clearer and Shop previews show other themes in their own colours.

guides.title: Capsule Machine
guides.summary: Spend tickets, Coins or Capsule Tokens on cosmetic prizes.

sections.heading: Pull options
paragraphs: The free daily capsule follows the game’s UTC date rollover. Use it separately from ticket, Coin or token pulls.

sections.heading: Guaranteed prizes
paragraphs: An Epic or better arrives at least every 10 pulls. A ten-pull purchase guarantees an Epic or better in that batch. Legendary odds start climbing after 60 pulls without a Legendary, and the 80th pull guarantees one. A Legendary resets its counter; Epic or Legendary prizes reset the Epic counter.

sections.heading: Weekly featured prizes
paragraphs: The banner features one Legendary and three Epic cosmetics. Half of Legendary pulls select the featured Legendary; half of Epic pulls select from the featured Epic group. The remaining selection favors unowned items over owned items.

sections.heading: Duplicates
paragraphs: Owned prizes turn into Coins instead of a second cosmetic. The history dots and rarity meters let you track recent pulls and guarantees. Use the Prize Counter if you prefer choosing an exact prize.

guides.title: Slots
guides.summary: Bet Game Corner Coins on a three-reel machine.

sections.heading: Playing
paragraphs: Open Events → Game Corner → Slots. Choose a bet of 10, 50, 200 or 1,000 Coins and spin. The bet is deducted first; any payout is added afterward.

headers: Payout as a multiple of the bet

sections.heading: Using your winnings
paragraphs: Spend Coins at the Prize Counter, use them for capsule pulls or save them for an exact cosmetic you want. A 1× payout returns the bet rather than making a profit.

sections.heading: Read the winning line (0.57.3)
paragraphs: Only the middle line pays. Cherry prizes count from the left reel. Winning symbols and the matching pay-table row light up, and the result shows the reason and payout at your bet. Reels now show their true stopped positions, so adjacent rows are not presented as wins.
Coins update when the reels stop. Auto ×10 keeps the bet you chose. On phones, Pay table sits beside SPIN; Slots also fits shorter windows.

guides.title: Prize Counter and Coin exchange
guides.summary: Buy the exact capsule cosmetic you want with Coins.

sections.heading: Capsule Tokens
paragraphs: One Capsule Token costs 1,000 Coins and provides one capsule pull. Tokens are used by the single-pull option.

sections.heading: Coin exchange
paragraphs: Buy 100 Coins for $5,000. Coins also come from Slots payouts and duplicate capsule rewards. Check your balance in the Game Corner header.

guides.title: Daily Field Research
guides.summary: Complete three daily tasks for money and items, then claim an extra reward for finishing the set.

sections.heading: Tasks and resets
paragraphs: Open Research to see your three tasks, progress and reward buttons. Tasks refresh daily at midnight UTC. Complete a task and press Claim; all three must be claimed to receive the completion bonus.

rows: Catch 3 Pokémon of the chosen type

sections.heading: Full set bonus
paragraphs: Claiming all three tasks awards five Ultra Balls, ten Great Balls and two Rare Candies.

guides.title: Achievements and titles
guides.summary: Reach long-term milestones to earn rewards, ribbons and trainer titles.

sections.heading: Achievement groups
paragraphs: Research includes Catching, Special looks, Battle, Raids + Tower, Islands + legends, Care + training, Collecting and Playtime. Milestones span catches, registered species, eggs, bosses, costumes, stamps, money and many other activities.

sections.heading: Titles
paragraphs: Achievements unlock named titles such as Rookie Hunter, Shiny Hunter, Stamp Collector and Professor’s Pal. Equip an earned title for your trainer profile. Check the achievement’s own description to see whether it counts current ownership or lifetime progress.

guides.title: Catch rules and automatic sorting
guides.summary: Choose which wild Pokémon your party catches, how balls are used and which duplicates stay.

sections.heading: What to catch
paragraphs: Open Catch to enable New species, Shiny, Void, Prismatic, Perfect IVs, Legendaries, New looks or Everything. Your party battles every encounter, but matching an enabled rule makes it attempt a catch.

sections.heading: Catch list
paragraphs: Add exact species, types or rarities you want to keep catching, even when already registered. An exact species entry does not automatically include its evolutions. Set a minimum IV percentage for catch-list catches if desired.

sections.heading: Keeping duplicates
paragraphs: Auto-send duplicates keeps the highest-IV copy of each species and look, sending eligible extras to the Professor. Favorites cannot be auto-sent, bulk-sent, released or Wonder Traded while starred. Party members, Day Care Pokémon, Megas, Founder Pokémon and fusions have additional protection. Review Never send categories and the species list before enabling duplicate cleanup.

sections.heading: Balls and manual battles
paragraphs: Choose the ball used for automatic catches, set separate Master Ball rules and configure automatic Poké Ball or Ultra Ball purchases. Rare finds can wait two minutes for you to battle them yourself before your team takes over.

sections.heading: Automatic selling
paragraphs: Auto-sell Nuggets converts found Nuggets into $1,000 and Big Nuggets into $5,000. Auto-sell spare balls lets you choose a stock target for each ball. Found balls above that target sell at half the Mart price. Bought balls stay, and the kept amount cannot fall below your auto-buy target.

sections.heading: Never send exact species
paragraphs: Catch → Never send → Species opens a list of up to 60 species. Add a species you have seen or caught, or toggle its lock on its Pokédex page. Auto-send and Send duplicates skip every copy of a listed species. The list is exact: protecting Bulbasaur does not also protect Ivysaur and Venusaur. Manual bulk sending can still ask you to confirm a listed Pokémon, so review its warning.

sections.heading: Evolution controls
paragraphs: Auto-evolve is on unless you turn it off. Turning it off makes eligible Pokémon wait with a green Ready to evolve arrow. Living dex and Use evolution items are optional switches, initially off; they are disabled while Auto-evolve is off. Living dex keeps the best copy of every species from evolving automatically. Use evolution items spends eligible stones and items from your bag. Read Evolution automation before enabling it.

sections.heading: Legendaries and bosses can call you first
paragraphs: Set Legendaries or Bosses to call me first to receive a call-out and chime before the automatic team takes over. You have two minutes to battle a Legendary yourself or arrange the team for a boss. Fight! begins the boss battle; Team first opens your party. Protected catches remain protected when the team takes over.

sections.heading: Family-wide catch lists (0.54.3)
paragraphs: Use the evolve-arrow control beside a species in the Catch list to include its evolution family. For example, choosing Beldum can also catch Metang and Metagross. Without that family option, the species entry remains specific.

sections.heading: Extra duplicate-send protections (0.54.4)
paragraphs: A Pokémon with Power-ups, your Buddy, or a nickname or Move Tutor move is never sent to the Professor as a duplicate. These protections apply alongside favorites and other protected Pokémon.

sections.heading: Costume and Event protections (0.57.0)
paragraphs: Catch → Never send includes a Costume option, enabled by default, to keep extra costume Pokémon. Event Pokémon and Pokémon in locked boxes are excluded from Send duplicates and auto-send. The PC’s Send action also excludes Event Pokémon. Costume and Event protections are distinct; review your rules before sending extras.
Catch everything ignores the Catch list’s minimum-IV filter. The minimum still matters when using the Catch list instead of Everything.

sections.heading: Spectral catching and protection
paragraphs: Spectral catching and Never send → Spectral are both initially enabled. Spectral can also be selected for Master Ball rules. Review these separately from Void, Prismatic and Costume. Hatch-all reveals are protected from premature auto-send in 0.57.3.

sections.heading: Auto-favourite (0.57.5)
paragraphs: Settings → Auto-favourite lets you select Shiny, Void, Prismatic, Spectral, Perfect and Legendary. New catches and hatches matching selected categories receive a favourite star. Existing Pokémon stay as they are. Favourites are protected from auto-send, Send duplicates, the Professor and Wonder Trade.

guides.title: Pokédex
guides.summary: Search species, track registration and explore the Pokémon found on each island.

sections.heading: Browsing
paragraphs: Open Pokédex and search by name or Pokédex number. Filter by island, registered species or species still missing. Seen-but-uncaught species appear as silhouettes; undiscovered species are hidden as ???. Small Shiny, Void and Prismatic markers show looks you currently own. Open a species to inspect its details.

sections.heading: Registration
paragraphs: Species stay registered after evolution, trading or transfer. Registration raises your rank and fills island checklists. A species being seen is different from owning or registering it.

sections.heading: Hunting from a species page
paragraphs: Use a species page to add it to your catch list. Once the Poké Radar is unlocked, eligible species can also be selected as Radar targets. Check whether its island is open before traveling.

sections.heading: Protecting a species
paragraphs: Use the lock on a species page to add or remove it from the Never send species list. That protection applies to the exact species, including extra copies; it does not cover the whole evolution family.

sections.heading: Registered and Seen filters (0.54.2)
paragraphs: Filter the Pokédex by Registered or Seen. The Looks view shows whether Shiny, Void and Prismatic variants have been registered for each species.

sections.heading: Skills book (0.54.4)
paragraphs: Open Skills in the Pokédex for one book containing every Signature Leader skill and every Ability, what each does, and which Pokémon have it.

sections.heading: Phone gestures (0.57.0)
paragraphs: Swipe left or right to turn Pokédex pages or move between Pokémon. Tap icons for their explanations. The phone layout supports portrait and landscape.

sections.heading: Seasonal collection and rarity filters
paragraphs: Spectral tracks species you have owned in that seasonal look. Search mythical, ultra beast or ub to find the newly distinguished labels; legendary remains a broader search. This is a label distinction, rather than new species or a battle balance change.

sections.heading: Wild Dex (0.57.5)
paragraphs: A separate Wild Dex counts eligible species you caught or hatched yourself, plus their evolved forms. Trades, market purchases, gifts and descendants with those sources in their family do not count. Earlier catches count; eggs hatched before the update lack the required family record. Earn Bronze at 100, Silver at 300, Gold at 600 and Master at 900 species.

guides.title: Poké Radar
guides.summary: Build a target chain for up to three times the Shiny, Void and Prismatic chances; stack it with rank and Shiny Charm.

sections.heading: Unlock and targeting
paragraphs: The Poké Radar opens with your sixth Gym badge. Pick a target from its Pokédex page, then hunt on that species’ island. The island must already be open.

sections.heading: Eligible targets
paragraphs: Ordinary species must have been seen or registered. Registered targets have a 30% Radar selection chance; seen but unregistered targets have a 10% chance. Legendaries must already be registered and awake on their island, and have a 5% selection chance. Mythicals cannot be targeted.

sections.heading: Charges
paragraphs: Each Radar Charge powers 25 successful Radar encounters. Only a successful Radar selection spends one encounter of charge and adds one to the chain. Ordinary encounters between Radar hits do not break it. Running out of charges pauses Radar hits without clearing the chain; another charge item lets it continue.

sections.heading: Chain shiny bonus
paragraphs: The multiplier is 1 + min(chain, 200) / 100. It boosts Shiny, Void and Prismatic chances equally, with a maximum of ×3 at chain 200. The chain can keep growing beyond 200, but the odds bonus stops growing.

The successful Radar encounter increments the chain before its rare looks are rolled: the first hit uses chain 1 (×1.01). The 30%, 10% and 5% target-selection rates above are separate from the chance of a rare look. An ordinary spawn of the same species does not receive the Radar bonus.

sections.heading: What stacks with the chain
paragraphs: Trainer rank sets the base odds. Shiny Charm multiplies the chance by 1 + 0.12 × charm level, up to ×2.8 at level 15. Radar then multiplies that chance again: maximum Charm plus maximum chain gives ×8.4 before live events.

Radar and Mass Outbreak bonuses are alternatives for an encounter. A successful Radar selection takes priority; it does not also receive the outbreak multiplier (×1 in 0.57.3). Neither increases the separate Perfect-IV roll.

For example, Rookie base Shiny odds of 1 in 2,400 become 1 in 800 at chain 200 without Charm. With Charm level 15 as well, they are about 1 in 285.71; Void is about 1 in 857.14 and Prismatic about 1 in 2,285.71. These examples exclude live events.
Active Shiny events also multiply these rare-look chances; crystal events add their multiplier to Void and Prismatic. Check the game’s current odds display for event-adjusted rates.

sections.heading: Keeping or resetting a chain
paragraphs: Selecting the same target again preserves its chain and best. Switching to a different target starts its chain and best at zero, while retaining remaining charge. Turning Radar off clears its target and chain. Flying to another island resets the current chain, including automatic island travel after a Gym.
The chain counts successful Radar encounters, rather than catches. A failed target-selection roll or a non-Radar encounter does not reset it.

sections.heading: Using the odds calculator
paragraphs: Choose Wild encounters, then Radar target, and enter the chain used for that roll, after the successful hit increments it. Enter 200 for any chain of 200 or more. The calculator reports odds conditional on a Radar hit and excludes live-event multipliers.

sections.heading: Looks label (0.57.0)
paragraphs: The Radar chain now labels its bonus as Looks. Looks ×3 means three times the Shiny, Void and Prismatic chances, rather than an extra catch, money or Perfect-IV bonus. The chain formula and Charm stacking above are unchanged.

sections.heading: Spectral rolls and recorded chains (0.57.3)
paragraphs: Radar also improves the seasonal Spectral base chance because it derives from the encounter’s Prismatic base. Rare finds retain the chain used at discovery, visible on their card and Discord. This recorded chain is historical; changing your current chain does not change that Pokémon.
Outbreak tuning in 0.57.3 is Looks ×1, replacing the old ×3. Radar and outbreak remain alternative encounter paths.

guides.title: Poké Mart
guides.summary: Buy supplies, permanent upgrades, evolution items and moves.

sections.heading: Departments
bullets: Poké Balls: buy balls as your rank unlocks them.
Healing: Potions, status cures, revives and PP restoration for battles you fight yourself.
Evolution: evolution stones and other items, including Linking Cord for species that normally evolve by trade.
Held items: browse general items and role-focused groups. Equip items from Party & PC.
Upgrades: permanent improvements to hunting, money, EXP and storage.
Move Tutor: teach compatible moves for money.
Bag & Sell: inspect items and sell treasure.

sections.heading: Useful distinctions
paragraphs: A Rare Candy raises a Pokémon by one level. Family Candy pays for power-ups instead. Nugget and Big Nugget sell for $1,000 and $5,000. Evolution items apply only to compatible Pokémon.

sections.heading: Planning purchases
paragraphs: Great Balls unlock at Bug Catcher rank and Ultra Balls at Ace Trainer rank. Use the item’s current price, compatibility and description before buying.

sections.heading: Large purchase confirmations
paragraphs: Purchases over $20,000 can ask for confirmation. Don’t show again suppresses that question. To restore it, press the bell beside your money in the Mart.

sections.heading: Phone purchasing (0.57.0)
paragraphs: Tap an item to open quantity choices ×1, ×5, ×10 and Max, then use the large Buy button. Check the displayed total before confirming.

guides.title: Permanent upgrades
guides.summary: Improve the hunt from the Mart’s Upgrades department.

rows: Faster wild encounters; starts at 14 seconds, ×0.95 per level, minimum 6 seconds
Shiny, Void and Prismatic odds ×(1 + 0.12 × level)
PC Pokémon receive 5% of party EXP per level, up to lead’s level
One extra free Poké Ball per upgrade level every 25 encounters
Starts at 6; +1 slot per level through 6, then +2 per level

sections.heading: Buying levels
paragraphs: Upgrade prices rise each level. Check NOW and NEXT to see the exact change before buying. Training Camp levels PC Pokémon only up to your lead’s level. Egg Basket capacity reaches 20 at its maximum level; Camping Gear reaches 1,020 closed-game battles.

sections.heading: Closed-game progress
paragraphs: Camping Gear sets the number of battles your party can simulate while the game is closed. It is a battle limit rather than a guarantee that the team defeats every opponent.

guides.title: Friends, trades and gifts
guides.summary: Add friends, share finds, trade Pokémon and battle together.

sections.heading: Adding friends
paragraphs: Open Friends and share your six-letter friend code. Add another code to send a request. Profiles show showcases, teams, cosmetics and Shelves. You can browse a friend’s PC and leave an offer that waits for them.

sections.heading: Live trades
paragraphs: Both trainers choose their Pokémon and confirm in the trade window. You can make five trades per day. Earn friendship points together to raise the Trade Level with that friend and unlock rarer trade categories. Both trainers must have reached the Pokémon’s island.

sections.heading: Rare trades and cooldowns
paragraphs: Legendary, Mythical, Void and Prismatic trades require at least five badges. A received Pokémon can be traded again 30 days after it arrived; its card shows the remaining wait. Founder Pokémon stay with their original trainer.

sections.heading: Gifts and battles
paragraphs: Send one gift per friend per day. Gifts can contain balls, treats and sometimes an egg. Gifts improve friendship for trading. Friend battles pit your party against theirs in an automatic fight. The rare-find feed supports reactions and offers.

sections.heading: Connection status
paragraphs: Friends, gifts, trading, battles and the Night Market pause while offline. Your ordinary hunt continues. The Friends page also shows how many trainers are online.

sections.heading: Favorite friends and gift shortcuts
paragraphs: Star a friend to keep them above unstarred friends in every sort and in Raid invitations, even when they are offline. Send all sends the day’s item gift to every eligible friend and reports how many were sent. Claim all in the Inbox opens every gift you can claim that day.

sections.heading: Daily gifts and protected favourites (0.54.5)
paragraphs: You can open up to 20 friend gifts per day. Favourited Pokémon must be unstarred before they can be traded or listed in the Night Market, matching their protection from Professor sends and Wonder Trade.

sections.heading: Phone trades and eligibility fixes (0.57.0)
paragraphs: Trade panels use full-screen phone layouts. On short windows the Pokémon cards shrink so Accept, Decline, Counter, Send offer and Confirm trade remain visible.

The release fixes eligibility problems affecting online catches and Day Care babies in trading and selling, including Wonder Trade for babies. Normal trade levels, fees, badge requirements, favourites and received-Pokémon cooldowns still apply.

sections.heading: Friendship points (0.57.3)
paragraphs: Trade Levels now use friendship points, not just opened gifts. Existing eligible activity counts retroactively. The days requirement remains 0 / 3 / 7 / 14 days for Levels 1 / 2 / 3 / 4; points required are 0 / 3 / 10 / 20. Point at the hearts, or tap them on a phone, for your level, unlocks, remaining days and points, and today’s contributions.

rows: Raid boss defeated in the same party

sections.heading: Cheers, re-trades and gift recovery
paragraphs: Use the heart in Friends’ finds to cheer each find once; eligible cheers grant a friendship point to both trainers, up to 3 per friend per day. Reactions lists who cheered your finds.

Received Pokémon now wait 30 days before another trade, replacing 14 days. Spectral uses the Void/Prismatic rare category. Gift claims explain failures and update the counter if gifts were already opened on another device. Send all no longer hides pending Inbox gifts, and duplicate friend rows were fixed.

sections.heading: Cheer all and friend battles (0.57.4)
paragraphs: Friends’ finds → Cheer all cheers every find you have not cheered yet, then reports the friendship points earned. The cap remains 3 cheer points per day with each friend.
Fused Necrozma, Kyurem and Calyrex now appear and fight in their fused forms in friend battles. The online count also supports friend lists above 1,000.

guides.title: Trainer card, Showcase and Shelf
guides.summary: Choose the profile your friends see.

sections.heading: Your card
paragraphs: Your trainer card displays your name, earned title, outfit, frame and card background. Events → Style contains the cosmetic wardrobe. Your Shelf below the card displays up to six dolls or decor pieces.

sections.heading: Showcase and team
paragraphs: Choose Pokémon for your Showcase to display favorite finds. Until you choose a Showcase, your party is used. Friends can open your profile, see your displayed Pokémon and team, and browse your PC.

sections.heading: Titles and collecting
paragraphs: Earn titles through Research achievements. Equip a title that matches your favorite activity, then decorate the card and Shelf to suit your collection.

sections.heading: Founder badge
paragraphs: Eligible Founders see their Founder badge on their own Trainer card as well as in the profiles and social screens shown to other players.

sections.heading: Change outfit from your card (0.54.4)
paragraphs: On your own trainer card, use the outfit button to open your outfits directly.

sections.heading: Show on Discord (0.54.5)
paragraphs: With the Discord app open, your Discord profile can show your current island, Tower floor or raid. After a Shiny, Void, Prismatic or Legendary catch, it can show that Pokémon for a few minutes. Turn it off in Settings → Show on Discord.

sections.heading: Stable Trainers board placement (0.54.5)
paragraphs: Trainers with the same score keep a consistent order. Your own row and rank remain visible even when you are outside the top 100.

sections.heading: Spectral statistics and rare-find details
paragraphs: Trainer statistics count Spectrals. Rare-find cards and Discord posts can show the exact odds recorded for that find, plus its Radar chain when applicable. A recorded find’s odds are historical, rather than a live prediction of your next encounter. Species/source eligibility can make the displayed find odds differ from a trait-only calculator.

sections.heading: Bug Hunter badges and player tags (0.57.5)
paragraphs: A bug report confirmed by the Tallgrass team earns a Bug Hunter badge after your Gym badges on your profile card. Each confirmed bug adds one.
A small grey friend-code suffix distinguishes players with the same name on boards, Raid screens, the Night Market, Friends’ finds and friend cards. Hover to see the full code.

sections.heading: World look counts (0.57.5)
paragraphs: Pokémon cards display how many of that kind exist worldwide for Shiny, Void, Prismatic and Spectral looks, including their combinations. These counts describe existing Pokémon, not the chance of finding one.

guides.title: Money, tickets, Coins and Glimmer
guides.summary: Different activities use different currencies; check the symbol before spending.

sections.heading: Family and Rare Candy
paragraphs: Family Candy is tied to an evolution family. Rare Candy is a bag item. The Lab exchanges one Rare Candy for three family Candy, or one for Legendary families.

sections.heading: Buying Coins
paragraphs: The Coin exchange sells 100 Game Corner Coins for $5,000. Check whether a direct Prize Counter purchase is preferable to a random capsule.

guides.title: Building your squad
guides.summary: Use a strong lead, useful bench roles and matching types to make four Pokémon work together.

sections.heading: Your four battle slots
paragraphs: The main squad uses up to four Pokémon. Slot 1 supplies your Leader skill. A Pokémon on the bench can still help through its Break or Support role.
bullets: Put a DPS Pokémon up front for damage.
Keep a Break on the bench to weaken wild foes and crack boss shields.
Keep a Support on the bench for healing and Guarded.
Open Synergies to see which type pairs and squad bonuses are active.

sections.heading: Prismatic and shiny teammates
paragraphs: At least one Prismatic grants +10% all stats to the party. Additional Prismatic do not multiply that party aura. Each shiny gives +15% battle money, up to three shinies (+45%). Balanced and the Prismatic aura multiply: together they give ×1.21 stats before other bonuses.

sections.heading: Guarded acts during the turn
paragraphs: Guarded intercepts the knockout damage and leaves the active Pokémon at 1 HP immediately. If it has not moved yet, it can still take its move that turn. This does not require full HP. The squad normally gets one use per fight; Light Clay allows two while the item’s effect is available. Sturdy remains an individual ability with its own full-HP condition.

sections.heading: Spectral in the team builder
paragraphs: The wiki team builder supports Spectral alongside Shiny, Void, Prismatic, Alpha, Perfect and Costume. Spectral affects the illustrated preview and is preserved in saved and shared squads. It adds no extra battle-stat bonus. Existing Spectrals remain valid after the season; only obtaining a new Spectral roll is seasonal.

guides.title: DPS, Break and Support
guides.summary: Every Pokémon has a role; rarity and power-ups strengthen what that role does.

sections.heading: Power-ups and held items
paragraphs: Each power-up adds 5% role strength. Big Root multiplies a Support’s bench healing by 1.5. Grip Claw multiplies a Break’s shield damage by 1.3. Wide Lens multiplies its guard-down catch bonus by 1.5.
bullets: Two Break Pokémon are useful against stubborn shields.
A Support must remain standing to keep helping from the bench.

sections.heading: Using Leader skills
paragraphs: Only slot 1 chooses the Leader skill. Mega and Gigantamax forms use the base Pokémon’s signature skill. Pokémon without one of these 40 skills get a type Leader skill instead: their primary type’s moves gain 15% at Common or Uncommon rarity, 18% at Rare, or 22% at Legendary.

paragraphs: Open Skills from the Pokédex for a combined reference to every Signature Leader skill and every species Ability, what each does, and which Pokémon have it.

guides.title: All 18 type synergies
guides.summary: Two squad members sharing a type activate that type’s squad bonus.

sections.heading: Activating a synergy
paragraphs: Each Pokémon counts once for each of its types. Two or more squad members of a type switch its synergy on; dual types can help activate two different synergies. Extra Pokémon of the same type do not provide extra copies of that synergy.
bullets: Weather synergies last five turns.
A Leader’s permanent weather takes priority over temporary type weather.
Use the Synergies panel to check which pairs are active before a hard fight.

guides.title: Damage, move coverage and type matchups
guides.summary: Matching your attack to a weakness matters more than simply choosing the highest-power move.

sections.heading: Physical and special moves
paragraphs: Physical attacks use Attack against Defense. Special attacks use Sp. Atk against Sp. Def. Nature, IVs, levels, variants, squad bonuses and held items change the stats used in a fight. An attack matching one of the user’s types gets a same-type bonus of ×1.5.

sections.heading: Full attacking type chart
paragraphs: Read across from the move’s type. Multiply both defending types together first, then apply Tallgrass’s super-effective or resistance adjustment.

sections.heading: Choosing moves
paragraphs: Check the damage preview and the target’s weaknesses. A lower-power super-effective move can beat a stronger neutral move. The Counter button helps find Pokémon with useful coverage.
bullets: Bring both good attacking coverage and safe defensive typing.
Speed usually decides who attacks first, though priority moves and other effects can alter order.
Moves consume PP; an empty move cannot be selected as an available attack.

guides.title: Shiny, Void, Prismatic, Alpha and Perfect
guides.summary: Rare looks can give real battle bonuses, and several can appear on the same Pokémon.

sections.heading: Shiny bonus: stats and battle money
paragraphs: The named Shiny bonus gives each shiny Pokémon +10% all stats. Having shinies in your active party also adds +15% battle money per shiny, capped at three. Boxed shinies do not contribute.
This party bonus does not improve encounter Shiny odds or the Radar chain. Use rank, Shiny Charm and the qualifying Radar or outbreak bonus for encounter odds.

sections.heading: Combined looks
paragraphs: Shiny, Void and Prismatic are separate traits in ordinary wild and Day Care rolls. Combinations such as Shiny Void or Void Prismatic are possible. A Prismatic can also be shiny and Void. Alpha and Perfect can occur alongside rare looks.

sections.heading: Void and Prismatic stats
paragraphs: Before other battle bonuses, Void multiplies non-HP stats by 1.2 and adds 0.4 × level to HP. Prismatic uses 1.3 and adds 0.6 × level to HP. A Pokémon with both uses 1.4 and adds 0.7 × level to HP. Integer rounding applies. The Prismatic party aura is an additional squad effect.

sections.heading: Names in older guides
paragraphs: Void was formerly called Umbral, and Prismatic was formerly called Prismana. These are the same traits under their current names.

sections.heading: Prism Aura does not stack (0.57.0 clarification)
paragraphs: A Prismatic in the party grants the party +10% all stats through Prism Aura. One is enough: additional Prismatic party members do not multiply or add another aura bonus. This is separate from the individual Pokémon’s Prismatic stat bonus.

sections.heading: Spectral seasonal look (0.57.2–0.57.3)
paragraphs: Spectral is a permanent ghostly cosmetic obtained during Spooky season. It stacks with the existing traits and has no additional combat-stat bonus. See Spectral Pokémon and Spooky season for availability, source-specific odds, breeding and trading.

guides.title: Wild shiny and rare-look odds
guides.summary: Rank and Shiny Charm improve rare-look odds; Radar and seasonal Spectral rolls have their own rules.

sections.heading: Base odds by rank
paragraphs: These are ordinary wild odds before Shiny Charm, Radar or outbreak bonuses. Void is one-third as likely as shiny; Prismatic is one-eighth as likely as shiny. Each trait is rolled separately.

sections.heading: Calculating your odds
paragraphs: If your rank’s shiny denominator is S and Shiny Charm level is C, your ordinary shiny chance is (1 + 0.12C) ÷ S. Void chance is that value ÷ 3; Prismatic chance is that value ÷ 8. Shiny Charm has 15 levels, so its maximum multiplier is ×2.8. It does not increase the Perfect-IV roll.

sections.heading: Target bonuses
paragraphs: In 0.57.3 an outbreak Pokémon gets ×1 shiny, Void and Prismatic chances (no additional look boost). A Radar-target encounter gets a multiplier of 1 + min(chain, 200) ÷ 100, up to ×3. These bonuses apply to the qualifying encounter, not every Pokémon you meet.

Rank and Shiny Charm stack multiplicatively with the target bonus. The Radar chain increments before the roll; chain 200 or higher gives ×3. Radar and outbreak do not stack with each other. See the Poké Radar guide for chain progression, resets and worked examples.
bullets: The number shown is a chance per eligible roll, not a guarantee after that many encounters.
Tower and Raid Eggs use their own odds; use their separate guides.

sections.heading: Live event odds and Tower events (0.55.0)
paragraphs: The odds display includes an active Shiny, Void or Prismatic event multiplier, for example “1 in 190 (2× event)”. Use the displayed rate for the current eligible roll.
Since 0.54.5, Shiny and crystal odds events also boost rare looks on Tower Route and Den floors.

sections.heading: Spectral and current outbreak tuning (0.57.3)
paragraphs: Spectral is a separate seasonal roll at 0.8 times the applicable Prismatic base chance, with its own Spectral-parent additions in Day Care. Eligible server-issued rolls and an active season are required. Use the Spectral filter in the calculator; it models the seasonal chance separately from the three older looks.

Important current-build change: the 0.57.3 installed outbreak tuning is Looks ×1, not the older ×3. Outbreaks still target an encounter species, but the calculator no longer applies an extra rare-look multiplier for them. Radar still reaches ×3 at chain 200.

guides.title: Natures and IVs
guides.summary: Nature changes two stats; IVs measure each Pokémon’s individual potential.

sections.heading: Reading IVs
paragraphs: Each of the six stats has an IV from 0 to 31. A higher IV raises that stat at the same level. The displayed IV percentage is the average IV divided by 31, rounded to a percentage. A Perfect Pokémon has 31 in every stat. Lucky Pokémon have all IVs between 28 and 31.
bullets: IV order: HP, Attack, Defense, Sp. Atk, Sp. Def, Speed.
100% is Perfect; 80% or higher is marked Great; 55% or higher is Good.
Judge the IVs that your moves actually use: a physical attacker benefits most directly from Attack.

sections.heading: Nature effects
paragraphs: A non-neutral nature raises one stat by 10% and lowers another by 10%. Neutral natures change neither.

sections.heading: Nature and individual-IV chances
paragraphs: An ordinary new nature roll selects one of 25 natures: 4% (1 in 25) for a particular nature. Each ordinary individual IV is selected from 0 through 31: 1 in 32 for a particular value before guaranteed Perfect or Lucky adjustments. These are separate from rare-look chances.

Day Care babies roll their own nature and IVs. Tallgrass’s Everstone stops evolution; it is not listed as a nature-inheritance item. Destiny Knot improves IV quality and the dedicated Perfect chance instead.
bullets: Changing Shiny Charm does not improve a nature roll.
Do not multiply a guessed natural six-perfect-IV rate into the dedicated Perfect odds; the Perfect bonus has its own listed probability.

sections.heading: Choosing a Pokémon
paragraphs: Compare the battle stats as well as the IV total. Level, evolution, typing, role, variants and power-ups all matter. A high Sp. Atk IV does not help a purely physical move.

sections.heading: Nature colors
paragraphs: A nature’s raised stat is green and its lowered stat is red. These colors mark the 10% nature modifier; they are separate from the green/red comparison between two Day Care parents’ IVs.

guides.title: Held item reference
guides.summary: Give a held item from Party & PC to tailor a Pokémon for damage, survival or bench support.

sections.heading: Using held items
paragraphs: A held item can strengthen battle stats, a role or a Leader skill. Check the description for whether the holder must be fighting, on the bench, or in slot 1. Destiny Knot is for Day Care; Everstone stops evolution.

sections.heading: Suggested items (0.54.2)
paragraphs: Use ITEMS beside AUTO under your party to see suitable held items from your Bag. The game previews proposed swaps before applying them and does not take an item held by another Pokémon.

sections.heading: Party effects and breeding clarification (0.57.0)
paragraphs: Luck Incense gives +25% battle money while held by a party member; additional Incenses do not stack. A Destiny Knot on either Day Care parent keeps the best of three fresh IV rolls and triples the dedicated Perfect chance. It copies no parent IVs, and two Knots do not stack.
Everstone prevents evolution and passes the holder’s nature to newly laid Day Care eggs. Eggs already in the basket retain their assigned nature.

sections.heading: Focus Sash timing fix (0.57.4)
paragraphs: Focus Sash now activates as the knockout hit lands: the holder survives at 1 HP and still makes its move. Previously it could skip that move before returning at 1 HP.

guides.title: Family Candy and power-ups
guides.summary: Spend a family’s Candy to strengthen a Pokémon beyond ordinary leveling.

sections.heading: What a power-up does
paragraphs: Each power-up adds 3% to all stats and 5% to role strength. A Pokémon can reach +10: +30% all stats and +50% role strength. Power-up bonuses stay with that Pokémon.

sections.heading: Getting Candy
paragraphs: Evolution families share Family Candy. Catching and other rewards add Candy to the matching family. Your Buddy can find Candy, and the Professor’s Lab converts Rare Candy into Family Candy.
bullets: Rare Candy can also raise a Pokémon by one level from the PC.
The Lab gives 3 Family Candy per Rare Candy for ordinary families, or 1 for a legendary family.
Check the shown Candy and money price before confirming a power-up.

guides.title: Catching and Catch rules
guides.summary: Set automatic rules for routine hunts and take control of special encounters when needed.

sections.heading: Manual and automatic catches
paragraphs: The manual Catch button uses your selected ball and displays its chance against the current Pokémon. Specialty balls are for manually fought battles. Automatic battles use Poké, Great, Ultra and Master Balls. Catch rules let you target new species, rare looks, Perfect Pokémon and other categories.

sections.heading: Improving a throw
paragraphs: Lower HP raises catch chance. Sleep or freeze applies a ×2.5 status multiplier; another major status applies ×1.5. Catching Charm gives ×(1 + 0.04 × level), up to ×2 at level 25. Break guard-down adds further catch chance during a fight.
bullets: Void, Prismatic and Legendary targets are harder to catch.
Ordinary throws cap at 95%; Master Balls always succeed.
A Quick Ball is strongest before attacking on turn 1.

sections.heading: Hunting duplicates
paragraphs: Catch list can target an exact species even if it is already registered. Set a minimum IV percentage to avoid spending balls on weaker duplicates. Available minimums include 50%, 70%, 80% and 90%. Categories can target types and rarities. Master Ball rules choose which rare encounters deserve one.

sections.heading: Stock management
paragraphs: Auto-buy maintains the chosen ball stock when you can afford it. Auto-sell spare balls sells found balls above your chosen limit at the Mart’s buy-back price. Bought balls stay, and auto-sell does not go below your auto-buy amount.

sections.heading: New Catch rules
paragraphs: Never send protects every copy of the selected species from automatic sending. Living dex keeps your best representative of each species from evolving automatically. Use evolution items lets available stones be used automatically. These choices start off until you enable them. Auto-evolve can also be switched off; those Pokémon wait under Ready to evolve.

sections.heading: IV-aware Professor send list (0.54.2)
paragraphs: Send duplicates and PC Select → Send show which Pokémon are selected, along with nature and IVs, ordered with the best IVs first. Review that list before confirming a send.

sections.heading: Protected duplicate catches (0.54.4)
paragraphs: Pokémon with Power-ups, your Buddy, and Pokémon with a nickname or Move Tutor moves are never sent to the Professor as duplicates.

sections.heading: Wait for the target to return (0.54.4)
paragraphs: A Poké Ball cannot be thrown while a wild Pokémon is in the air, underground or underwater during Bounce, Fly, Dig or Dive. Wait for the Pokémon to come back before attempting the catch.

guides.title: Every Poké Ball and its bonus
guides.summary: Choose a ball whose condition matches the encounter.

3× from 7pm to 6am on your clock, or anytime on Misty Pyre.
3.5× on Sunny Shore or on a Water type.
(41 − level) ÷ 10 below level 30, with a minimum of 1×; 1× at level 30 and above.
2× if your Pokémon is higher level, 4× at twice the target’s level, 8× at four times.
4× if the target has base Speed 100 or more.
