sections.heading: Unlocks and shopping
paragraphs: More ball choices unlock as you earn Gym badges. The Mart has separate ball shelves. Check the live chance beside the manual Catch button rather than assuming the ball’s multiplier is the final probability.

sections.heading: When a wild Pokémon cannot be hit by a ball (0.54.4)
paragraphs: You cannot throw a Poké Ball while a wild Pokémon is out of reach during Bounce, Fly, Dig or Dive. Wait for it to return before throwing.

guides.title: Boss shields and battle reports
guides.summary: Use Break to open the shield, DPS to exploit it, and Support to survive.

sections.heading: Shield flow
paragraphs: Break bench effects damage shields every two turns. When a shield breaks, the boss is staggered for three turns. A normal shield then regrows at half its maximum; Binding Band extends the broken period to five turns and makes a normal shield regrow at one quarter. Iron Shell regrows fully.
bullets: Shatter increases the next qualifying DPS hit by 50%; Zoom Lens makes it double instead.
Scope Lens is designed for attacks during a broken shield.

rows: Every 3 turns, deals 15% of the active Pokémon’s max HP.
Keep a Support alive on the bench.
From turn 18, Attack and Sp. Atk rise, then rise again every 5 turns.
Improve early damage and super-effective coverage.

sections.heading: Reading a battle report
paragraphs: The report separates damage, shield breaking and healing. Its advice can point out a shield that never broke, insufficient healing, low party levels or missing super-effective moves. Use those clues to change the squad instead of repeating an unchanged losing fight.

sections.heading: No-hit battle timeout (0.54.1)
paragraphs: A battle ends after ten consecutive turns in which neither side can land a hit. A wild opponent flees without causing a loss; Gym and Tower encounters count the timeout as out of turns.

guides.title: Day Care and breeding pens
guides.summary: Pair compatible Pokémon to produce eggs while you hunt.

sections.heading: Starting a pair
paragraphs: Open Day Care and drag two Pokémon into the open pen. The parents gain a little EXP every wild encounter, but do not evolve while in Day Care. Each pen has its own timer; all pens share the Egg Basket.

rows: Purchase in the Glimmer Shop after every island is done, or at Professor rank (0.57.5)
Compatible; produces an egg every 50 wild encounters.
Compatible; produces an egg every 100 wild encounters.
Compatible; produces an egg every 100 wild encounters.
No shared family, type or Ditto

sections.heading: What hatches
paragraphs: The baby is the first stage of its selected parent’s evolution line. With Ditto, it follows the other parent. With two non-Ditto parents, one parent’s family is selected. Day Care babies hatch at level 5. A full basket pauses production until space is available.

sections.heading: Comparing parent IVs
paragraphs: Each parent now shows all six IVs side by side. Green is higher than the other parent; red is lower; equal values are neutral. Right-click a parent to open its full Pokémon card. The comparison helps assess the parents; it does not copy higher individual IVs into the baby.

sections.heading: Evolution after leaving Day Care (0.54.3)
paragraphs: A Pokémon taken out of Day Care does not immediately evolve automatically. It waits until its next level-up, or you can choose Evolve manually.

sections.heading: Everstone and nature inheritance (0.54.4)
paragraphs: A Day Care parent holding an Everstone passes its nature to every baby. The Day Care also explains the Everstone and Destiny Knot effects.

sections.heading: Parent natures and inheritance help (0.54.5)
paragraphs: Each Day Care parent now shows its nature. The help panel summarizes Ditto compatibility, Destiny Knot stacking, Everstone nature inheritance, and how Shiny, Void, Prismatic and Alpha traits pass down.

sections.heading: Nature timing and egg fixes (0.57.0)
paragraphs: Eggs already in the basket keep the nature assigned when they were laid. Changing a parent or its Everstone later does not change those eggs.

The 0.57.0 notes report fixes ensuring Everstone and Destiny Knot apply to every eligible egg, and that Day Care babies can enter selling, trading and Wonder Trade normally. Existing requirements, protections and cooldowns for those features still apply.
On a phone, tap a parent and then a pen slot rather than dragging. Hold the parent to open its actions.

sections.heading: Spectral parents and hatch protection (0.57.3)
paragraphs: Spectral parents improve the seasonal Spectral egg chance. Select their Spectral trait in the breeding builder; existing eggs keep the traits assigned when laid. Auto-send no longer sends a hatch awaiting its reveal before you see it. Hearth and Nanny pickers adapt to the space above them, including short phone screens.

sections.heading: Fifth breeding pen (0.57.5)
paragraphs: Buy the fifth pen in the Glimmer Shop after completing every island or reaching Professor rank. It adds another breeding pair; the earlier four pen unlocks remain.

sections.heading: Hatch Rush (0.57.5)
paragraphs: During a live Hatch Rush, egg production runs 2× or 3× faster and eggs hatch 2× or 3× sooner. The golden egg banner and Egg Basket area show the active event. Each egg keeps the same rare-trait odds.

guides.title: Breeding rare looks and Perfect Pokémon
guides.summary: Parents add rare-trait chances; different islands and Destiny Knot offer separate bonuses.

sections.heading: Base egg chances
paragraphs: Day Care eggs start with 1.5× the ordinary wild shiny, Void and Prismatic chances for your rank and Shiny Charm. Parents caught on different islands double this base rare-look chance again. The two parents’ catch regions matter, not their names or language.

rows: +1 in 64 Alpha chance; two Alpha parents give 1 in 32

sections.heading: Destiny Knot
paragraphs: A Destiny Knot on either parent triples the Perfect-IV chance, including the Perfect-parent additions. It also selects the best total IV spread out of three rolls for a non-Perfect baby. Two Destiny Knots do not give another multiplier. This is Tallgrass breeding; it does not use the standard five-inherited-IV rule.

sections.heading: Example
paragraphs: At Rookie rank without Shiny Charm, an ordinary Day Care egg has 1-in-1,600 shiny odds. One shiny parent adds 1-in-128, for about 1-in-118.5 overall. Different-island parents double the base part to 1-in-800; with one shiny parent the total is about 1-in-110.3.

sections.heading: Checking your pair
paragraphs: The odds strip beside your selected pen shows its current shiny, Void, Prismatic, Perfect and Alpha chances. Its tooltip also estimates the average hunting time. An average is not a deadline; a dry streak can be much longer.

sections.heading: IV comparison versus Perfect inheritance
paragraphs: A higher parent IV display does not make that individual IV pass down. The Perfect-parent addition is for the game’s designated Perfect trait. A naturally high or rounded 100% IV display alone is not the special parent bonus. Destiny Knot still improves the baby’s IV selection and triples the dedicated Perfect chance.

sections.heading: Odds events affect Day Care eggs (0.54.3)
paragraphs: Shiny and crystal-odds events also apply to eggs laid in Day Care. The game update notes do not specify a changed numeric event multiplier for eggs, so use the event's displayed odds rather than assuming an extra multiplier.

sections.heading: Everstone nature inheritance (0.54.4)
paragraphs: A parent holding an Everstone passes its nature to every baby. The Day Care now explains what Everstone and Destiny Knot do.

sections.heading: IVs and nature are set for each egg (0.57.0)
paragraphs: Destiny Knot keeps the best of three new IV rolls; it copies no individual IV from either parent. One Knot is enough. The separate Perfect chance multiplier is unchanged.
An egg already laid keeps its assigned nature even if you change the parents or Everstone before hatching. Version 0.57.0 fixes item application to every eligible egg.

sections.heading: Spectral inheritance (0.57.2–0.57.3)
paragraphs: During an active Spooky season, the Spectral base is the Day Care Prismatic base ×0.8, plus 1/1,280 for each Spectral parent. Use Spectral parent counts, not Prismatic parent counts, for this addition. The different-island bonus doubles the base part only. Live event multipliers are separate. Outside the season, parents do not create new Spectral eggs.

guides.title: Hatching, Hearth and Nanny
guides.summary: Eggs warm during wild encounters; a warmer or Nanny can make the process easier.

sections.heading: The Hearth
paragraphs: Place a Fire-type on the Hearth to warm eggs without using a battle slot. A Fire-type warms eggs 1.5× faster. A Pokémon with Flame Body, Magma Armor or Steam Engine warms them 2× faster. A warmer in the party also works. Only the best warmer counts; they do not stack.

sections.heading: The Nanny: every current interval
paragraphs: The strongest rare-look reduction applies. Shiny makes the interval 10% shorter, Void 15% shorter and Prismatic 20% shorter. Combined looks use the best reduction; the reductions do not add or multiply. Alpha, Perfect and costume do not shorten the Nanny timer.

sections.heading: Opening eggs
paragraphs: A ready egg waits in the basket until you hatch it. A Nanny opens ready eggs one at a time and can work while the game is closed through offline hunting. Open all eggs in the Professor’s Lab quickly reveals every ready egg, including Raid and Costume Eggs.

sections.heading: Hatch-screen and count fixes (0.57.0)
paragraphs: Welcome back, What you missed, What’s new and the hatch reveal now appear one at a time to prevent competing screens from blocking clicks. The egg card’s All action, Open all and reveal count agree. Eggs becoming ready during a reveal join it instead of restarting the reveal.

sections.heading: Hatch all counts and reveal protection (0.57.3)
paragraphs: The hunt egg card, Hatch all count and tooltip, Day Care basket and reveal count the same eggs that can open now. Other eggs are explicitly marked as still warming. Auto-send does not remove a newly hatched baby before its waiting reveal is shown. Hearth and Nanny pickers fit small windows.

sections.heading: Hatch Rush speed (0.57.5)
paragraphs: The team-run Hatch Rush event makes Day Care eggs arrive 2× or 3× faster and hatch 2× or 3× sooner. Check its active multiplier and countdown. It does not improve the rare-look probability per egg.

guides.title: Egg Basket capacity and overnight breeding
guides.summary: Basket upgrades hold more eggs; special eggs have their own space rules.

sections.heading: Basket lanterns and special eggs
paragraphs: Each Basket lantern adds two more spaces. Raid, gift and event eggs do not count toward the Day Care basket limit and do not stop when that limit is full.

sections.heading: Away limit
paragraphs: While away or idle, Day Care stops at 25 waiting eggs and unrevealed hatches combined. Basket lanterns raise this limit by two each, up to 31. The egg indicator says FULL; hatch or reveal some and production resumes.

sections.heading: A practical overnight setup
bullets: Fill each unlocked pen with a compatible pair.
Choose a warmer for the Hearth and a Nanny for automatic hatches.
Buy enough basket space for the time you will be away.
Clear ready eggs and unrevealed hatches when you return.

guides.title: The Tower: Climb and Daily
guides.summary: Start small, build a team during the run, and bring one recruit home.

sections.heading: Unlock and start
paragraphs: The Tower opens with your 3rd Gym badge. In Climb, choose one Pokémon from the PC. It starts as the first stage of its line at level 5 while keeping its look, IVs and nature. Your normal Pokémon is not permanently reset. Build a run party of up to six as you catch wild opponents.

sections.heading: The floor loop
bullets: Fight each battle yourself.
Gain levels and learn moves as you climb.
Choose one of three reward options after each floor.
Every 10 floors, choose a route through the next section.
Use run items and recruits to replace weaknesses in your squad.
When the run ends, choose one Pokémon caught during the run to take home.

rows: A wild Pokémon to defeat or catch.
Trainer battle with more money and a better reward.
A stronger, higher-level wild Pokémon with better rare-look chances; legendaries appear deeper in.
No battle; restores 60% party HP and revives fainted members.
No battle; a free reward with better rarity odds.

sections.heading: Daily Tower
paragraphs: Daily gives everyone the same starting squad and floors. It begins at level 5 and ends after 50 cleared floors. Compare your result on the friends board. Climb also records a weekly best; the week runs Monday to Sunday in UTC.

sections.heading: Floor stat boosts (0.54.3)
paragraphs: Each Tower floor displays its stat boost as Tower boost +X% stats. Opponents continue to gain strength beyond level 100.

sections.heading: Moves offered after Tower evolution (0.55.0)
paragraphs: When a Tower Pokémon evolves, its move choices include moves learned by the new form at level 1 or below the current evolution level. The update notes give Swampert (Earthquake and Hammer Arm) and Volcarona (Heat Wave) as examples.

sections.heading: Leaderboard saving and display (0.57.5)
paragraphs: Runs upload as soon as they end. The end screen reports Saving, Run saved to the board or a retry state. Failed uploads retry automatically, including after restart; click the status to retry immediately.

Runs ending with five or six Pokémon now upload with the whole party. Missing personal-best and weekly-best records upload automatically on this version. Each friends board shows its top 50 in pages that fit the window, and keeps your own row and place visible. Desktop empty-row and phone layout problems are fixed.

guides.title: Tower Luck, recruitment and run items
guides.summary: Rare teammates improve Luck; recruits and temporary items help you keep climbing.

sections.heading: Wild rare looks
paragraphs: In a regular Tower wild encounter, the rare-look thresholds scale with 1 + Luck ÷ 4. The Prismatic threshold is that multiplier ÷ 6,000, Void is ÷ 1,800 and shiny is ÷ 300. Den encounters multiply these thresholds by three. These are ordered alternatives: Prismatic is checked first, then Void, then shiny. They are not independent combined-look rolls.

sections.heading: Recruiting
paragraphs: Recruitment uses balls found during that run. A stronger species can reduce its catch chance; check the percentage on its ball button. A full run party opens the swap screen so you can choose who makes room.

sections.heading: Items for the run
paragraphs: Healing, Candy, held items, Mega Stones, vitamins and charms can appear as rewards. Held items can be passed between run squad members. Vitamin rewards raise a stat by 8% per dose. Expert Belt rewards add 12% squad damage, up to three. A Healing Charm restores 15% HP after each floor. Golden Poké Balls increase the number of offered rewards.

sections.heading: Spectral and fainted vitamins
paragraphs: Tower Spectral chance uses its own seasonal roll at 0.8 times the raw Prismatic threshold for the selected Luck and room. At Luck 0 in a regular room this is 1 in 7,500. It can coexist with the one selected Shiny/Void/Prismatic look. Version 0.57.2 also fixes vitamins not working on fainted Tower Pokémon.

guides.title: Tower rewards and taking a recruit home
guides.summary: Your cleared floor determines the end-of-run payout.

sections.heading: Run payout
paragraphs: For F cleared floors, the money payout is 25F² + 300F. Bounty Tickets are floor(F ÷ 5). Rare Candy is 2 × floor(F ÷ 10). The result screen pays out the floors you completed, including when you choose to leave.

sections.heading: Milestones
paragraphs: Climb best-floor milestones at 25, 50, 75 and 100 each award a Costume Egg once. Finishing Daily records the day’s floor and score.

sections.heading: Take-home choice
paragraphs: At the end, choose one of your recruits. Its level is capped by your main adventure’s current level limit. Claim the result to finish the run and receive its prizes. Your run’s temporary inventory and party are separate from the main adventure.

guides.title: Raids and friend parties
guides.summary: Fight a 5★ boss with a prepared four-Pokémon squad and optional friends.

sections.heading: Unlock and passes
paragraphs: Raids open with the 5th Gym badge and need an online connection. You receive 10 free passes each UTC day. Extra passes cost 60 Glimmer, with up to 10 purchases a day and a total of up to 20 raid bosses per day. A pass is used whether you win or lose.

sections.heading: Party rounds
paragraphs: A raid party holds up to four trainers. Invite friends and use each round to contribute damage. Each trainer hits once per round. A round ends when everyone has hit or after five minutes. The boss and party state come from the online raid screen; check its current timer before joining.

sections.heading: Prepare your squad
paragraphs: Raid battles use four Pokémon. Keep Break and Support useful: Break opens shields, while a standing Support can block the boss’s Big Attack. Use the estimate and damage preview to compare coverage, Leader skills and squad order before spending a pass.

rows: Your squad fights for up to 30 turns.
Every 6 turns; a standing Support blocks it. Without one, it damages the active Pokémon and the bench.
At turn 20, the boss’s Attack and Sp. Atk rise.
Use Break to expose the boss, then DPS to exploit the opening.

sections.heading: Defeat rewards
paragraphs: A contribution of at least 2,000 credited damage earns the defeat bonus: $5,000, 2 Rare Candy, 13 Family Candy and 6 Bounty Tickets. The top damager in a party gets a crown, one extra Raid Egg and 1.5× bonus money. Raid Eggs remain valuable even when your contribution misses the defeat-bonus threshold.

sections.heading: Raid invitation eligibility (0.55.0)
paragraphs: The invite list only includes friends who have unlocked raids with five Gym badges. A count under the list shows how many friends are not eligible yet.
Raid party invites show their remaining time. Search the invite list by trainer name or friend code; online friends appear first. Leave party is available as a direct button.

sections.heading: Phone squad controls (0.57.0)
paragraphs: Tap your Raid squad to edit it on a phone. Tap a Pokémon to pick it up and then its destination slot; hold a Pokémon for its actions. The first-turn restrictions on Fake Out and First Impression also apply to automatic Raid battles.

sections.heading: Two bosses per UTC day (0.57.3)
paragraphs: Bosses rotate every 12 hours: a Mythical at 00:00 UTC, then a Legendary or Ultra Beast at 12:00 UTC. The roster cycles through the eligible bosses. The card previews the next boss and remaining time. A party already fighting at the change has 30 minutes of grace to finish.

These are two roster slots per day, not a reduction of the separate pass or run limits. Completing a boss with a friend in the same Raid party adds 2 friendship points, for up to 3 qualifying wins per day with that friend. The invite list and next-page control were repaired in 0.57.2.

sections.heading: Held-item tips and Suggested squad (0.57.4)
paragraphs: Each Pokémon in the Raid squad shows its held item. A glowing recommendation identifies a better item in your Bag for the current boss; hover for the reason and use Equip all to apply the recommendations.

Suggested squad tests candidates against the exact boss, tries type pairs for Synergies and selects suitable held items from your Bag. The update retains the previous suggestion as a minimum; if the stronger choice depends on items, Equip all brings in that squad with its items. Spectral Ghostly dodge does not apply in Raids.

sections.heading: Pass-aware invitations and spectator HP fix (0.57.5)
paragraphs: Friends with no passes left today appear in a No passes today group and cannot be invited; eligible friends are listed first.

Party members who only watch no longer inflate boss HP. A member who skips their first round removes their share of boss HP, but can still join in and attack later. The defeat card now fits the smallest phones.

guides.title: Raid Eggs, damage milestones and Master Balls
guides.summary: Raid Eggs give unusually strong rare-look odds without Day Care parents.

sections.heading: Damage and extra eggs
paragraphs: Raid damage milestones award extra eggs at 10,000, 20,000, 35,000 and 50,000 damage. Your personal damage matters for these milestones. Friend-party results can add another egg for the top damager. Read the result’s credited damage and egg total before claiming.

sections.heading: Master Ball reward
paragraphs: A 50,000-damage hit qualifies for the raid Master Ball reward. Raids award at most one Master Ball per day in the full-launch rules.

sections.heading: Hatching
paragraphs: Raid Eggs are ready to open from the Egg Basket or Open all eggs in the Professor’s Lab. They do not take ordinary Day Care basket spaces. They roll their own traits; Day Care parent bonuses and Destiny Knot do not apply.

sections.heading: Spectral Raid Eggs
paragraphs: During active Spooky season, an eligible Raid Egg has an independent 1-in-375 Spectral chance before live odds events. The existing Shiny, Void, Prismatic and Perfect rolls remain separate.

guides.title: Species abilities and Leader skills
guides.summary: A Pokémon’s ordinary ability and its squad Leader skill are different effects.

sections.heading: Two different ability systems
paragraphs: A Pokémon’s ordinary species ability belongs to that individual and can affect its own battle actions. The squad Leader skill comes from slot 1 and modifies the squad. Some share a name but have different effects: Typhlosion’s Flame Body Leader skill boosts Fire moves and squad Speed, while ordinary Flame Body is a contact-trigger burn ability and also helps egg warming.

Drizzle / Drought / Sand Stream / Snow Warning
Set rain / sun / sand / snow when entering.
Swift Swim / Chlorophyll / Sand Rush / Slush Rush
Double Speed in rain / sun / sand / snow.
Adds one priority to status moves.
Multiplies moves of 60 power or less by 1.5.
Multiplies power by 1.3 for moves with chance-based secondary effects.
Multiplies physical Attack by 1.5 while statused.
A contact attacker loses 1/8 of its max HP.

Blocks supported indirect damage, including burn, poison and sand damage.

sections.heading: Reading ability descriptions
paragraphs: Check battle messages and the Pokémon card for its actual ability. Ability descriptions describe the named ability; squad Leader descriptions explain a separate squad bonus. Do not treat matching names as extra copies of the same effect.

sections.heading: Skill book in the Pokédex (0.54.4)
paragraphs: The Pokédex Skills button opens one reference containing every Signature Leader skill and every Ability, their effects, and the Pokémon associated with each.

sections.heading: Ruin abilities and Paradox boosts (0.55.0)
paragraphs: Wo-Chien, Chien-Pao, Ting-Lu and Chi-Yu identify which stat their Ruin ability weakens when they enter battle.

Protosynthesis and Quark Drive raise the Pokémon’s highest stat in harsh sunlight or Electric Terrain: Speed rises by 50%, while other stats rise by 30%. The battle reports the boost, which ends when the weather or terrain ends. These effects do not apply in raids.

sections.heading: Stamina fix (0.57.4)
paragraphs: Stamina also raises Defense when the Pokémon damages itself in confusion.

guides.title: Starter odds: all looks and combinations
guides.summary: Ordinary starters have their own fixed odds, separate from wild encounters and Founder rewards.

sections.heading: Ordinary starter traits
paragraphs: Every one of the 27 regular starter choices uses the same roll. Your starter begins at level 7. Rank, Shiny Charm, parents, Radar and outbreaks do not change this roll.

sections.heading: Exactly each starter look
paragraphs: This table requires the listed looks and excludes the other Shiny, Void or Prismatic looks. For example, “Shiny” here means shiny without Void or Prismatic.

sections.heading: Combined traits, allowing extra looks
paragraphs: Inclusive combinations allow an additional look. “Shiny + Void” includes both ordinary Shiny Void and the three-look combination.

sections.heading: Perfect and Alpha
paragraphs: The ordinary starter has no dedicated Perfect bonus roll and no Alpha roll. Its IVs and nature are its own. The separate guaranteed Founder reward should not be counted as an ordinary starter result.

sections.heading: Founder starter
paragraphs: The Founder thank-you reward is a once-only Prismatic starter with perfect IVs and a Founder Ribbon. It is not shiny, Void or Alpha in this reward path. Its appearance is fixed by the reward; Shiny Charm does not upgrade it.

sections.heading: Every Shiny Charm level
paragraphs: Levels 0 through 15 all leave starter odds unchanged: Shiny 1 in 16, Void 1 in 48 and Prismatic 1 in 128. The full level selector in the odds reference shows the same starter chances at each level.

sections.heading: Spectral starters during Spooky season
paragraphs: During the active season, an eligible ordinary starter can independently be Spectral at 1 in 160. The New Game screen displays this chance. It can coexist with the existing starter looks. For example, Shiny + Void + Prismatic + Spectral, allowing extras, is 1 in 15,728,640 before any supported live event multiplier. The older exact-look table above leaves Spectral unspecified; use the calculator to require or exclude it.

guides.title: Every Shiny Charm level
guides.summary: See how each upgrade changes rare-look chances and which sources it affects.

sections.heading: The complete upgrade ladder
paragraphs: Shiny Charm multiplies Shiny, Void and Prismatic probabilities, plus the seasonal Spectral base on supported sources. It does not multiply Perfect or Alpha, or a parent’s fixed trait addition. A +120% bonus means 2.2 times the original chance, not a 120% probability.

sections.heading: Every rank and every variant
paragraphs: The odds reference includes all 192 rank-and-Charm combinations: 12 ranks and levels 0–15. Choose a rank, Charm level and source to see Shiny, Void, Prismatic, their combinations, Perfect and Alpha where available.

rows: Current ×1 multiplier; uses ordinary rank and Charm odds.
1.5× wild base, plus parents and different-island bonuses.
3× ordinary wild base; Perfect fixed at 1 in 100.
Ordinary wild chances; not the Costume Egg multiplier.

guides.title: Combining rare-look odds
guides.summary: Know the difference between a trait chance, an exact look and a combination that allows extra traits.

sections.heading: Three ways to read a percentage

rows: Any shiny result, including shiny with other looks.
Shiny and Void, but not Prismatic.
Shiny and Void, whether Prismatic is absent or present.

sections.heading: Independent looks
paragraphs: Ordinary wild encounters, ordinary starters, Day Care eggs, gift eggs, Costume Eggs and Raid Eggs roll their look traits separately. To require several traits together, multiply their probabilities. To forbid a trait, multiply by its failure probability instead. Leave a trait out of the calculation if you do not care whether it appears.
bullets: Shiny + Prismatic, extras allowed: shiny chance × Prismatic chance.
Exactly Shiny Prismatic: shiny chance × Prismatic chance × (1 − Void chance).
Three looks together: shiny chance × Void chance × Prismatic chance.
No rare look: (1 − shiny chance) × (1 − Void chance) × (1 − Prismatic chance).
At least one rare look: 1 − chance of no rare look.

sections.heading: Perfect and Alpha combinations
paragraphs: When a source offers an independent Perfect or Alpha roll, include its probability the same way. Day Care can produce Alpha through Alpha parents. Ordinary wild look rolls, regular starters and Raid Eggs do not add an Alpha roll. The Perfect percentage in this reference is the dedicated Perfect bonus, not a guessed probability of naturally obtaining six maximum IVs.

sections.heading: Tower is different
paragraphs: Tower wild looks use one ordered choice. It checks Prismatic first, then Void, then shiny. A newly generated Tower wild Pokémon cannot independently roll two or three of these looks together. A starter you brought into the Tower can keep a combination it already had.

sections.heading: Modifiers do not all stack
paragraphs: Radar targets and outbreak replacements are alternative encounter paths. A Radar target does not receive both Radar and outbreak bonuses. Day Care different-island bonuses double only the base look part before parent additions. Destiny Knot affects Perfect and IV quality, not shiny or other look chances. Hearth and Nanny affect time, not chance per egg.

sections.heading: Seven traits and 128 exact variations
paragraphs: Spectral adds a seventh trait to Shiny, Void, Prismatic, Perfect, Alpha and Costume. The calculator lists all 128 exact patterns, subject to source restrictions and seasonal availability. The older three-look examples leave Spectral unspecified unless you require or exclude it.

Tower still chooses at most one of Shiny, Void and Prismatic, but Spectral is an additional independent seasonal roll. A Tower Spectral can therefore also be shiny, Void or Prismatic, while two of those three older looks remain mutually exclusive.

guides.title: Special rewards, Alpha and source-specific odds
guides.summary: Raids, costumes, prize encounters and bosses each use different rules.

rows: Rank plus parents; Knot can triple

sections.heading: Bosses that join you
paragraphs: After a victory, a boss may join without a normal catch. The chance depends on the defeated boss type. These are chances per victory, not encounter frequencies. Joined bosses do not roll Shiny, Void or Prismatic. Alpha status is built into Alpha and Mega Alpha bosses.

sections.heading: Bounty and event rewards
paragraphs: Check whether the prize is a Costume Egg or a costume encounter. An egg uses Costume Egg chances; an encounter uses its encounter chances. A costume name alone does not identify the odds.

sections.heading: Chance of catching is a separate question
paragraphs: Rare-look odds describe what appears or hatches. Catch chance depends on ball, remaining HP, status, species catch rate, legendary status, variants, Catching Charm and guard-down effects. Improving catch chance does not make a rare look more likely to appear.

guides.title: Terrains and Surge abilities
guides.summary: Electric, Grassy, Psychic and Misty Terrain change grounded Pokémon’s battle conditions.

sections.heading: Terrain rules
paragraphs: A Surge ability sets its matching terrain on entry for five turns. Hadron Engine sets Electric Terrain. A newly set terrain replaces the previous one. Terrain and weather can exist together. These terrain mechanics apply to ordinary battles, Gym and boss fights, Tower and player battles; raids keep their separate battle rules.

sections.heading: Grounded Pokémon
paragraphs: Flying-type Pokémon, Pokémon with Levitate and Pokémon currently airborne using Fly are not grounded. Most terrain protections and move bonuses apply only to grounded Pokémon.

rows: Grounded users’ Electric move power ×1.3; grounded Pokémon cannot be put to sleep.
Grounded users’ Grass move power ×1.3; grounded Pokémon heal 1/16 max HP each turn; Earthquake, Bulldoze and Magnitude hit grounded targets at half power.
Grounded users’ Psychic move power ×1.3; protects grounded targets against qualifying priority moves.
Grounded targets take half-power Dragon moves and resist new major status conditions and confusion.
Sets Electric Terrain on entry; Special Attack ×4/3 during Electric Terrain.
In Electric Terrain, its highest stat is boosted:×1.5 for Speed or×1.3 for a relevant attacking/defending stat.
Sets Grassy Terrain after the holder takes a surviving hit.
Power doubles against a grounded target in Electric Terrain.
Power×1.5 for a grounded user in Psychic Terrain, in addition to the terrain’s ordinary Psychic boost.

guides.title: Ditto, Transform and Imposter
guides.summary: Ditto can copy the opponent’s combat form while keeping its own HP.

sections.heading: Transform
paragraphs: Ditto has access to Transform. Using it copies the opponent’s species and types, non-HP battle stats, current stat stages, moves and ability. Copied moves receive 5 PP each. Ditto keeps its own maximum HP and current HP rather than copying the foe’s HP.

sections.heading: Imposter
paragraphs: A Ditto with Imposter attempts Transform when it enters the battle. It cannot transform into a fainted foe, while already transformed, or while the foe is in an invulnerable phase such as Fly. Transform is temporary: switching out restores the original form, moves and ability.

sections.heading: Where it applies
paragraphs: Transform and Imposter use the expanded battle rules outside raids. Transformation changes the current battle only; it does not change Ditto’s Day Care species, family, nature, IVs or breeding compatibility.

sections.heading: Wild Ditto appearance fix (0.57.0)
paragraphs: A wild Ditto using Transform now displays the copied Pokémon’s appearance while retaining the name Ditto. This visual fix does not turn the captured Ditto into the copied species.

guides.title: Mega Evolution, Dynamax and Gigantamax
guides.summary: Mega items change your Pokémon during battle; giant bosses use the correct Dynamax or Gigantamax appearance.

sections.heading: Preparing a Mega Evolution
paragraphs: A Pokémon’s Mega chip shows its compatible stone. The Can Mega Evolve filter finds eligible species, and earlier stages say which evolution can Mega Evolve. Give the correct stone or other transformation item in the PC. A Pokémon that still needs to evolve cannot use a later stage’s stone as though it were that species.

sections.heading: When your Pokémon transforms
paragraphs: The active holder builds charge as it fights: one per completed turn, plus another if it lost HP during the turn. It transforms before its next action once it has at least three charge. Only one transformation is used by your squad in that fight. Switching to another holder does not create a second use.

sections.heading: What changes
paragraphs: The transformed form uses its own species stats, typing and ability, with your Pokémon’s level, genes, rare looks and squad bonuses. The change preserves its HP percentage and compatible remaining move PP. Some forms also map moves to their form’s move set. The ordinary form returns after the fight. Mega, Primal, Origin and other item-triggered forms are named by the item’s transformation.

sections.heading: Wild transformations
paragraphs: An eligible ordinary wild Pokémon has a 6% chance to appear transformed; an eligible Legendary or Mythical uses 10%. This chance is separate from Shiny, Void, Prismatic and Perfect rolls. Defeating or catching a transformed wild Pokémon awards its corresponding transformation item.

sections.heading: Dynamax versus Gigantamax
paragraphs: A giant boss without a genuine Gigantamax form is labeled Dynamax. Only species with a real Gigantamax form use the Gigantamax presentation. Both belong to the giant-boss category, with the same giant-boss battle and join rules. A giant boss joining you gives its ordinary Pokémon; the giant appearance is not a sixth rare-look roll.

guides.title: PC boxes, moving and protecting Pokémon
guides.summary: Organize your collection, move Pokémon into your party and keep selected boxes untouched by automatic sorting.

sections.heading: Moving Pokémon
paragraphs: Open Party & PC. Drag a Pokémon to an empty party slot to add it, or onto another slot to swap. Drag a party member back to the PC list to remove it. Double-clicking a Pokémon adds or removes it from the party. Hold a dragged Pokémon over a box arrow to carry it to another box.

sections.heading: Box organization
paragraphs: Each box holds 30 Pokémon. The PC keeps an empty box waiting at the end and has no fixed box limit. Rename a box, choose its wallpaper and lock it to reserve it. New catches and automatic sorting skip locked boxes, but you can still move Pokémon into one yourself. Use Apply to all boxes in the wallpaper picker to reuse the selected wallpaper throughout the PC.

sections.heading: Bulk actions
paragraphs: Press Select to choose several Pokémon. Ctrl-click adds or removes individual selections; Shift-click selects a range; Ctrl+A selects the current box; Esc clears the selection. On a search page, select the page or all results. Move to… fills empty slots in the chosen box, then later boxes with room. Existing Pokémon are not swapped out.

sections.heading: Sorting and duplicate transfers
paragraphs: More contains Send duplicates and Auto-sort boxes. Sort by Pokédex number, rarity, rare looks, newest, strength or type. Pin an order with Keep sorted to sort new catches automatically. Duplicate transfers keep your best copy of each species, look and costume, respecting Catch protections.

sections.heading: Favorites, nicknames and comparison
paragraphs: Mark favorites and give Pokémon nicknames from their PC card; nicknames can be up to 12 characters. When your party is full, Swap in… lets you select who makes room and compare both Pokémon’s battle stats, total and IVs.

sections.heading: Sprites and nature colors
paragraphs: Use the HD or Pixel sprite button on the box bar to choose the sprite style. Opening a Pokémon’s card plays its cry when sound is enabled. Stat labels highlight the nature’s raised stat in green and lowered stat in red.

sections.heading: Move a whole box (0.54.2)
paragraphs: In the PC Boxes list, drag one box onto another to move the whole box and all of its Pokémon.

sections.heading: Touch moves and send protections (0.57.0)
paragraphs: On a phone, tap to pick up a Pokémon and tap its destination; tap it again to cancel. Hold it for Move, Card and Info.
Send duplicates and auto-send skip Event Pokémon and Pokémon in locked boxes. PC Send also leaves Event Pokémon out. Never send → Costume, initially on, protects extra costumes.

sections.heading: Card and Bag windows (0.57.0)
paragraphs: A card action that navigates to the Shop, Lab or Buddy closes the card so the destination is visible. Esc cancels a nickname edit. The Bag and other windows opened from a card appear above it; closing those windows returns to the card.

sections.heading: Persistent sprite style and fusion recovery
paragraphs: The Pokémon card’s Pixel / HD selection is remembered across cards. Card HD displays the HD sprite even if the PC view uses Pixel. Version 0.57.3 fixes fused Kyurem, Necrozma and Calyrex disappearing from the PC after saving. Update before investigating missing fused-form entries; do not reset your adventure.

guides.title: PC search and filters
guides.summary: Combine search words to find Pokémon by level, IVs, moves, rare looks, items and more.

sections.heading: Use search with sorting
paragraphs: Choose a Show filter and a sort order to narrow the results further. Holding an item includes Mega Stones and orbs. Select a result and use Show in its box to clear the search and return to its storage location.
