sections.heading: IV sorting and low-IV searches (0.54.3)
paragraphs: Sort IVs high-to-low or low-to-high. Search with queries such as iv<20 or <20% to find low-IV Pokémon.

sections.heading: Spectral, Mythical and Ultra Beast filters
paragraphs: Search spectral or spooky for the seasonal look. Mythical, ultra beast and ub work in the PC and Pokédex; the PC Show filter includes Mythical and Ultra Beast. A broad legendary search still matches all these high-rarity categories.

guides.title: Saved teams and counter teams
guides.summary: Keep named parties ready for different hunts and enemies.

sections.heading: Saved teams
paragraphs: Use the Teams row in Party & PC to save your current party under a name. You can keep up to ten presets and rename or delete them. Loading a team restores its available Pokémon in the saved order. Pokémon that have left your collection or are at Day Care are skipped.

sections.heading: Counter teams
paragraphs: A counter-team action builds a party from available Pokémon for the selected opponent. Your previous party is remembered, and Undo restores the available members. Counter teams exclude Pokémon in Day Care. Check the selected Leader, moves and held items before committing to the battle.

sections.heading: AUTO for the current island
paragraphs: The AUTO button below your party proposes a party from your whole PC for the current island’s Gym and wild encounters. It considers matchups, levels, Power and IVs. Review the proposed party before confirming. Your Buddy stays; Founder Pokémon stay unless you allow the proposal to move them into the PC. Your previous party can be restored with Undo.

guides.title: Moves, pins and the Move Tutor
guides.summary: Inspect your Pokémon’s moves, choose its four-move set and teach compatible extra attacks.

sections.heading: Learning moves
paragraphs: Open a Pokémon in Party & PC and choose Moves. Its available moves include level-up moves, previously taught moves and its current set. Moves show their type and Physical, Special or Status category.

sections.heading: Pins and automatic choices
paragraphs: Pin moves you want to keep. Up to four pins fit a move set. Swap a current move for another available move when you want more control, or use automatic moves to clear pins and let the game choose again.

sections.heading: Teaching moves
paragraphs: Open Mart → Move Tutor, choose a Pokémon and inspect its compatible moves. Teaching costs money and adds the move to that Pokémon’s learned pool. False Swipe and Hold Back cost $5,000; qualifying sleep and paralysis catch moves cost $4,000. Other move prices vary, so check the displayed cost.

sections.heading: A catching move set
paragraphs: False Swipe or Hold Back helps avoid knocking a target out. Sleep and paralysis improve catching. Keep at least one useful damaging move too, and check Ghost immunity before relying on False Swipe.

sections.heading: Move category filters
paragraphs: The Tutor has Physical, Special and Status buttons. Select one to show only that category, then press it again to return to all categories. Sort by Strongest, Physical / Special / Status, Cheapest or A–Z. These filters help you match attacks to a Pokémon’s stronger attacking stat.

sections.heading: Gigaton Hammer (0.54.4)
paragraphs: Gigaton Hammer cannot be used on two consecutive turns. Use another move between Hammer attacks.

sections.heading: Stone Axe and Blood Moon (0.55.0)
paragraphs: Stone Axe is a Move Tutor move Kleavor can learn. A successful hit leaves pointed stones that hurt each Pokémon entering the opposing side.
Ursaluna can learn Blood Moon from the Move Tutor. It cannot be used on consecutive turns; use another move between Blood Moon attacks.

sections.heading: Self-Destruct and Explosion (0.54.5)
paragraphs: Self-Destruct and Explosion make the user faint; Damp prevents this. In raids, a Pokémon that uses either move is out for the rest of that raid. Automatic teams keep these moves for low-HP situations.

sections.heading: First-turn moves and touch details (0.57.0)
paragraphs: Fake Out and First Impression only work on that Pokémon’s first turn after entering battle. Automatic hunting, Tower, Raids and friend battles avoid using them later; manual battle buttons are disabled with an explanation when ineligible.
Move details stay inside the battle text area so hovering no longer shifts the buttons. On a phone, hold a move to read its details and tap battle text for the log.

guides.title: Evolution and evolution choices
guides.summary: Evolve Pokémon from their PC card, with level, item, gender and day-or-night requirements.

sections.heading: How to evolve
paragraphs: Open a Pokémon in Party & PC → Evolution. The card lists available evolutions and usable items, and a green arrow marks a ready Pokémon. With Auto-evolve on, eligible ordinary Pokémon evolve by themselves; special looks and Perfect Pokémon wait for confirmation. Turn Auto-evolve off to make all eligible Pokémon wait for manual evolution. Living dex can also preserve your best copy of each stage. An Everstone blocks automatic level evolution.

sections.heading: Items and branches
paragraphs: Use the matching evolution item from the card. Linking Cord handles evolutions that normally require trading. Some branches let you pick the result from Evolution once the level requirement is met. Check the species page for its particular method rather than assuming the rules from another Pokémon game.

rows: At Good Buddy or level 20, choose Espeon or Umbreon; Sylveon also requires a Fairy move. Leaf Stone gives Leafeon; Ice Stone gives Glaceon.
At level 7, the Evolution choice lets you pick a branch.
At level 20, pick the available branch from Evolution.
At level 53, pick the available branch from Evolution.
Evolving into Ninjask also creates Shedinja when you have a spare Poké, Great or Ultra Ball.
Evolves into Alcremie at Good Buddy or level 20.

sections.heading: Gender and time
paragraphs: Vespiquen, Wormadam, Salazzle and Froslass require females; Mothim and Gallade require males. Lucario, Roselia, Tyrantrum, Gumshoos and Lurantis have day requirements. Chimecho, Aurorus, Houndstone and Frosmoth have night requirements. Night runs from 7 pm to 6 am on your local clock.

sections.heading: Costumes
paragraphs: A costume can restrict evolution unless it has a matching evolved costume. Read the costume note on the Evolution tab before planning to evolve it.

sections.heading: Friendship and branching evolutions
paragraphs: Good Buddy can unlock an eligible friendship evolution without waiting for level 20. Gender and day-or-night requirements still apply where specified. Eevee’s manual Evolution choices include Espeon and Umbreon at Good Buddy or level 20, with Sylveon also requiring a Fairy move. A Linking Cord lets Clamperl choose Huntail or Gorebyss.

sections.heading: Evolution row and updated cries
paragraphs: Version 0.57.3 fixes Evolution row alignment and supplies cries for Lycanroc, Wishiwashi, Oricorio and 19 more Pokémon, including relevant Mega and Crowned forms. These are presentation fixes.

guides.title: Mega Evolution, special forms and Gigantamax bosses
guides.summary: Equip the matching transformation item to let a compatible Pokémon transform during battle.

sections.heading: Giving a transformation item
paragraphs: Open Party & PC → Evolution and give the matching Mega Stone or special item from your bag. It has a separate slot from the ordinary held item. The Pokémon transforms on its own mid-battle and returns to its usual form afterward. Take returns the transformation item to your bag.

rows: Fused Dusk Mane or Dawn Wings Necrozma

sections.heading: Finding stones and items
paragraphs: Mega bosses can drop their transformation item. Wild Legendary Pokémon that have a transformation item can change during the encounter; these transformed encounters drop their item. Check the item entry and Mega Stone reference for the exact compatible species.

sections.heading: Dynamax and Gigantamax bosses
paragraphs: Large shielded bosses are called Gigantamax only when the species has a real Gigantamax form. Other giant bosses are called Dynamax. These giant bosses first enter the possible island-boss pool at Ashen Peak. Prepare Break support for their shields. Their boss appearance is separate from the matching Mega or special-item transformations equipped through the PC.

sections.heading: Reading the Mega chip
paragraphs: Pokémon cards, Hunt cards and the PC show a Mega or special-form chip with the matching item icon. Point at it to see the transformation and item details. A Pokémon whose later evolution can Mega Evolve shows the relevant evolved species instead. The PC’s Can Mega Evolve filter helps find current candidates.

guides.title: Fusion: Kyurem, Calyrex and Necrozma
guides.summary: Combine compatible Legendary Pokémon with a reusable fusion item, then split them again later.

sections.heading: How to fuse
paragraphs: Open the base Pokémon’s Evolution tab in Party & PC and choose a compatible partner. You need the listed reusable fusion item. Take both Pokémon out of Day Care and finish any pending hatch reveals first. Pokémon offered in a trade cannot fuse; remove incompatible Mega items before trying.

sections.heading: What happens
paragraphs: The partner is stored inside the fusion and leaves its separate party or PC position. The result shows the combined special looks of both Pokémon. Review the preview before confirming. Fusions cannot be sent to Day Care or transferred away as ordinary single Pokémon.

sections.heading: Splitting
paragraphs: Use Split on the Evolution tab to restore both Pokémon. The base Pokémon’s original rare looks return, and the partner returns to your collection. The fusion item is reusable.

sections.heading: Ultra Necrozma
paragraphs: Fuse Necrozma with Solgaleo or Lunala first, then equip Ultranecrozium Z so the fused Necrozma can use Ultra Burst in battle.

sections.heading: Fused walking sprites (0.57.0)
paragraphs: Dawn Wings and Dusk Mane Necrozma, White and Black Kyurem, and the Calyrex riders now walk in their fused forms instead of showing an unfused walking sprite.

sections.heading: Saved fused-form fix (0.57.3)
paragraphs: The release fixes fused Kyurem, Necrozma and Calyrex disappearing from the PC after a save. This is separate from the 0.57.0 fused walking-sprite fix.

guides.title: Buddy friendship and daily hearts
guides.summary: Choose a companion that walks behind you, finds items and grows closer through daily activities.

sections.heading: Choosing and changing
paragraphs: Open Buddy and pick an owned Pokémon. It can walk with you without taking a party slot. You can change to a new Buddy three times per day; returning to one you already used that day is free. Each Pokémon keeps its own heart progress, and No buddy lets you walk alone. The day resets at midnight UTC.
Trading a Pokémon starts its Buddy hearts over for the receiving trainer.

sections.heading: Six daily hearts
paragraphs: Each Buddy can earn one heart from each task, for up to six hearts per Pokémon per day.

rows: Meet 40 wild Pokémon with it as Buddy
Win 10 route battles with it in your party
Catch 5 Pokémon while it is Buddy
Click your Buddy on the route or its card
Bring it into a Raid battle or a Tower climb

sections.heading: What it finds
paragraphs: Buddy finds include its family Candy, Great Balls, Super Potions, Nuggets, evolution stones, Rare Candy and Big Nuggets. Higher friendship finds things more often and improves Rare Candy selection. Best Buddy also earns a ribbon and pink sparkle. Friends see your Buddy on your card and PC visits.

sections.heading: Friendship evolutions
paragraphs: A Pokémon’s earned Buddy hearts can unlock an eligible friendship evolution at Good Buddy. Check its Evolution tab after reaching that tier; some species still have additional time, gender or move requirements.

guides.title: Weather and time of day
guides.summary: Weather and the local clock influence the scene, encounter mix, some balls and certain evolutions.

sections.heading: Day and night
paragraphs: Night is 7 pm through 5:59 am on your local clock. Day begins at 6 am. Time-sensitive evolutions and Dusk Ball use these periods.

sections.heading: Wild encounter mix
paragraphs: Weather shifts wild selection toward matching types: Rain favors Water and Electric; Sun favors Fire and Grass; Sand favors Rock, Ground and Steel; Snow favors Ice; Fog favors Ghost, Psychic and Fairy. Night favors Ghost, Dark and Poison and reduces some daytime-friendly encounters. Weather is selected by island and hour.

sections.heading: Catching and evolution
paragraphs: Dusk Ball works at night, or on Misty Pyre at any hour. Check each ball’s entry for its bonus. A few evolutions require day or night, so revisit a ready Pokémon at the correct time.

sections.heading: Route-wide event weather (0.57.4)
paragraphs: Live surprise events can place rain, thunderstorms, snow, a blood moon or the aurora over every route. Check the active event and countdown instead of relying only on the ordinary island weather table.

guides.title: Hunt log, Interrupt and manual battles
guides.summary: Follow encounters, inspect your active Pokémon and take over a wild battle yourself.

sections.heading: Reading the Hunt log
paragraphs: Hunt log shows your fighting Pokémon or lead, the current wild Pokémon and a What happened feed. The feed lists catches, evolutions, rewards and other events with timestamps. Use its page arrows to browse older entries. Boss and Gym fights can add a report with damage, shields, healing, turns and suggestions after a loss.

sections.heading: Taking over
paragraphs: Use Interrupt on the strip to battle a wild Pokémon your team is fighting. In Settings or Catch, enable Battle rare finds myself to make Shiny, Void, Prismatic and new costume finds wait two minutes for you. If you do not take over, the team continues automatically.

sections.heading: In battle
paragraphs: Choose moves, switch party members, use compatible battle items and select a ball to catch an eligible wild target. The Catch button shows the selected ball’s chance against that opponent. After the manual encounter, the ordinary hunt resumes.

sections.heading: Waiting encounters
paragraphs: The wild card shows whether a Pokémon is waiting for you, an outbreak encounter or a prize encounter. If nothing is active, it shows the next encounter countdown or the number waiting.

sections.heading: Calls and preparation
paragraphs: Legendaries and island bosses have separate call me first controls in Catch rules. A boss call offers Fight! or Team first so you can inspect or change your party. Calls wait two minutes before the team resumes automatically.

sections.heading: Phone battles and first-turn moves (0.57.0)
paragraphs: Phone battles fill the screen with large type-coloured move buttons. Tap the battle text to open the log and hold a move for its details.
Fake Out and First Impression are available only on the user’s first turn out. Later turns show disabled move buttons and the reason; automatic teams also respect this restriction.

guides.title: Rush, resting and closed-game progress
guides.summary: Process waiting encounters and understand what changes when Tallgrass is hidden or closed.

sections.heading: Rush
paragraphs: After your first badge, Rush can process waiting encounters together. A normal charge handles up to 25 encounters; two charges can be stored, with one charge returning every 45 minutes. The button shows how many waiting Pokémon it will process. Bosses, Gyms and rest periods can prevent Rush.

sections.heading: Hidden versus closed
paragraphs: On desktop, Hide sends Tallgrass to the tray while the team keeps hunting at full speed. Close saves and exits completely. Closed-game progress runs at one-third the normal pace and stops at the battle cap set by Camping Gear.

sections.heading: Away catch-up
paragraphs: On returning, away progress can be processed in batches of up to 30 without spending normal Rush charges. Camping Gear starts at a cap of 120 closed-game battles and adds 60 per level.

sections.heading: Fainted Pokémon
paragraphs: A fainted party member sits out briefly and returns with half its HP. If the whole available party goes down, the team rests before hunting again. Use the HP and rest indicators to see when it can fight.

sections.heading: Bosses while hidden
paragraphs: When Tallgrass is hidden in the desktop tray, the team hunts at full speed and can complete automatic boss and Gym battles. With Bosses set to call me first, a boss waits for your response. When the app is completely closed, closed-game catch-up runs at one-third speed and bosses and Gyms wait for you. The return summary distinguishes these cases.

sections.heading: Update while away and Rush charges (0.54.5)
paragraphs: An update notice offers Restart now or Not now before restarting. A required update can restart while you are away; the game applies the hunting progress accumulated while it waited when it opens again.
The hunt strip and Rush button show remaining charges and when the next charge returns.

sections.heading: Cloud save catch-up and the 0.56.1 fix
paragraphs: When switching devices, Play here loads your latest account progress before hunting resumes. Time already played on another device is not counted again as away progress.
Version 0.56.1 fixes the documented freeze after closing the 0.56.0 welcome-back card and improves catch-up performance for large collections.

sections.heading: Phone background progress (0.57.0)
paragraphs: After switching to another app on a phone, the game credits full-speed hunting for the first 2 hours and then uses the normal away pace. It uploads the save when you switch away. This phone rule differs from the desktop tray and completely closed desktop rules above.

sections.heading: Crash-rest recovery and hunting fixes (0.57.1–0.57.3)
paragraphs: Version 0.57.2 fixes Pokémon Center rest timers lasting hours after a crash or clock change. A full-party rest normally lasts 60 seconds. Update to a current build before considering any save repair.

Version 0.57.1 repairs walking without encounters after 0.57.0. In 0.57.2 hunting continues rather than waiting for slow roll delivery. Rush explains why it stopped and when a boss is next; 0.57.3 includes further hunt timing fixes.

guides.title: Settings, sound and help
guides.summary: Adjust sound, sprites, rare-find alerts and the strip’s appearance.

sections.heading: Sound
paragraphs: Sound and cries controls battle sounds, fanfares and cries. Volume adjusts loudness. Special alerts is separate: it can chime for waiting rare finds, boss rematches or Gym challenges even with ordinary sound off.

sections.heading: Look and strip
paragraphs: HD sprites switches between smooth sprites and original pixel sprites. Scene displays the island diorama; Clear leaves the trainer and walking team without the background. Modular strip Size changes its drawing scale. Opacity controls how transparent the strip and panels are when you are not pointing at them.

sections.heading: Window controls
paragraphs: Always on top pins Tallgrass above other windows when the platform supports it. Desktop settings can also offer Start with Windows, Use all monitors and Hardware acceleration. Hardware acceleration changes take effect on the next launch. These desktop options depend on the platform you are using.

sections.heading: Help and recovery
paragraphs: Settings includes Patch notes, Welcome tour, Squads and Suggestions. Reset layout returns the strip to the bottom center, closes panels and restores their sizes while preserving the game and settings.

sections.heading: Starting over
paragraphs: Start a new game begins a fresh adventure and keeps the previous save as a backup. Treat this as a restart rather than a layout repair; use Reset layout for misplaced windows.

sections.heading: Taskbar and saved monitor layouts
paragraphs: On Windows, Taskbar button & Alt-Tab gives Tallgrass an ordinary taskbar button and an Alt-Tab entry. The tray icon continues to work. Panel positions and monitor settings persist across updates; windows placed on another monitor are remembered. Available desktop controls depend on the platform.

sections.heading: Redeem a code and Support
paragraphs: Use Redeem a code for official reward codes. Support opens the game’s Patreon page; the game’s support link states that everything in the game remains free.

sections.heading: Desktop window recovery (0.54.1)
paragraphs: The desktop game stays on screen. If the window is misplaced, use the tray menu → Reset position.

sections.heading: Cloud save and Classic fullscreen (0.56.0)
paragraphs: Settings → Help → Cloud save opens saving and account-backup controls. The scene’s cloud icon opens the same feature.
In Classic mode, F11 expands the game window to fullscreen. Press F11 again or Esc to restore its previous size.

sections.heading: Rare finds in the Discord (0.57.0)
paragraphs: Show my rare finds in the Discord controls whether especially rare catches, such as a Shiny Void, can be shared in the Tallgrass Discord’s rare-finds channel with your trainer name. Turn it off to keep those finds private. This is separate from Show on Discord, which controls Discord profile activity.

sections.heading: Updates and browser installation (0.57.0)
paragraphs: Settings → Help → Patch notes shows the installed version. On PC, Updates checks for a newer version and can restart into it. On a phone, Settings → This browser → Install explains how to add the game to the home screen.

sections.heading: Current troubleshooting and recorded finds
paragraphs: Use the latest update for the rest-timer, freeze-input, gate-loading and hunting repairs documented in 0.57.1–0.57.3. Rare-find displays can show recorded odds and the Radar chain used for that find. Card sprite style is remembered independently from the PC sprite view.

sections.heading: Display and performance fixes (0.57.4)
paragraphs: Use all monitors now stays enabled after updates and restarts. The Game Boy theme performance issue is fixed; online checks also use less data while the game is untouched.

sections.heading: Auto-favourite (0.57.5)
paragraphs: Automatically star new catches and hatches matching selected Shiny, Void, Prismatic, Spectral, Perfect or Legendary categories. The setting does not retroactively star Pokémon already owned.

guides.title: Classic and Modular layouts
guides.summary: Choose one window with tabs or movable floating panels.

sections.heading: Classic
paragraphs: Classic puts the game in one main window with a tab bar. Choosing a tab or a Poké Ball menu item changes the screen in that window. Drag the window’s edges or corners to resize it.

sections.heading: Modular
paragraphs: Modular opens each menu item as its own panel. Open several, move them around and resize them independently. The strip keeps the hunt visible while panels are closed. Drag the strip to move it and its side grips to change width.

sections.heading: Recovering a layout
paragraphs: Use Settings → Layout to change modes. Reset returns the strip and panels to their default positions and sizes. Always on top controls whether other windows can cover the game when supported.

sections.heading: Platform differences
paragraphs: Desktop window behavior depends on the desktop app. An Android wrapper can expose its own Float and return-to-app controls; use the controls supplied by the Android version rather than assuming desktop tray or multi-monitor features are available.

sections.heading: Layout after updates
paragraphs: Saved panel positions and monitor choices persist through updates. Reset layout remains available for windows you want returned to their default sizes and positions. On Windows, Taskbar button & Alt-Tab can make the game easier to bring forward alongside the tray icon.

sections.heading: Official phone layout (0.57.0)
paragraphs: The official browser game uses a hunt strip at the top and bottom navigation for Hunt, Party, Events, Day Care and More. It adapts to portrait and landscape. Phone panels and pop-ups fit the screen, with their own close controls. See Playing on a phone for gestures and installation.

guides.title: Saves, Discord and cloud sync
guides.summary: Keep the same adventure across devices with Discord cloud saves, local backups and offline progress.

sections.heading: Your account save and local copy
paragraphs: From 0.56.0 onward, Tallgrass can sync your adventure to your Discord account across Windows, Mac and the official browser game. A local copy still protects progress while offline. Use the Cloud saves and device switching guide for save choices, transfer and restoration.

sections.heading: Starting on a new device
paragraphs: Log in with the same Discord account. A new installation can offer the existing account save or a fresh adventure. If both devices already have progress, compare the two saves before deciding; the unchosen copy is retained as a backup.

sections.heading: Online access and offline play
paragraphs: Social features such as friends, trades, gifts, Raids, Wonder Trade and the Night Market need a connection. Ordinary offline hunting can continue; its local save uploads when the game reconnects. Signing out keeps the local save.

sections.heading: One active device per account
paragraphs: Use Play here on the device you want to continue with. It loads the latest account save and pauses the other device. Catch-up only counts time when no other device was playing.

sections.heading: Recovery and backups
paragraphs: Settings → Help → Cloud save manages account copies. Restore a backup can show local or account copies depending on platform. Keep unreadable save files and backup copies before attempting recovery. Reset layout affects windows; Start a new game begins a fresh adventure.

sections.heading: Discord email verification
paragraphs: If Discord reports an unverified email, use Discord’s account settings to verify that email, then retry login. Phone verification and age checks do not replace email verification.

sections.heading: Updates and startup fixes
paragraphs: Check the game version after updating. Version 0.56.1 fixes the documented 0.56.0 welcome-back freeze. Platform wrappers may update their native shell separately from game content.

sections.heading: Official phone support (0.57.0)
paragraphs: The official site supports phone layouts and home-screen installation. Sign in with the same Discord account to use your existing adventure. The first-start browser notice now explains the shared cloud save. The iPhone installed web app has a short-code login flow.

sections.heading: Paused devices and first browser login
paragraphs: When another device is active, this hunt stops moving, the route dims and a Paused chip identifies the active device. Play here transfers the active session.

If no account save exists, the browser explains this and offers Import a save file or Start a new game. To upload an existing PC save, open Tallgrass 0.56.1 or newer online on that PC once. The browser automatically offers the account save when it arrives. The gate-loading screen also recovers from interrupted connections in 0.57.2.

guides.title: Choosing a starter and Founder gifts
guides.summary: Pick a starter to begin the adventure; eligible pre-launch testers also have a separate Founder reward.

sections.heading: Your starting Pokémon
paragraphs: The game offers starter Pokémon from Kanto through Paldea. Your chosen starter begins at level 7 in Dewleaf Town. You also receive $300, 20 Poké Balls, five Great Balls and three Potions. A starter’s combat role and later evolutions can help decide which one suits your preferred party.

sections.heading: Founder reward
paragraphs: Pre-launch testers recognized as Founders can choose one of the 27 starters as a Prismatic with perfect IVs, a Founder Ribbon and their Founder number. This is a separate thank-you reward for eligible accounts. It needs an online connection to claim.

sections.heading: Founder restrictions
paragraphs: Founder Pokémon stay with their original trainer forever. They cannot be traded or sent away. The Founder badge and numbered ribbon identify the reward; ordinary starter rolls are a separate system.

sections.heading: Spectral and starter-screen fixes
paragraphs: Ordinary starters show the seasonal Spectral chance of 1 in 160 during Spooky season. The Founder reward remains a separate fixed reward. Version 0.57.2 fixes click-through after freezes and starter screens whose Choose button fell outside small or zoomed windows.

guides.title: Sending money to friends
guides.summary: Use Send gold to give a friend money when gold trading is available online.

sections.heading: Sending
paragraphs: Open the friend’s profile and choose Send gold. Enter an amount or use a quick amount button, review the recipient and press Send. You need the money in your own balance and an online connection.

sections.heading: Receiving limit
paragraphs: A player can receive up to $1,000,000 per day. The panel shows how much more that friend can receive today. Max is limited by your available money and their remaining allowance.

sections.heading: Availability
paragraphs: Gold trading is an online feature and may be disabled temporarily. If sending fails, the amount is returned to your balance. Money gifts are separate from daily item gifts and Pokémon trades.

guides.title: Auto-evolve, Living dex and item evolution
guides.summary: Control which Pokémon evolve automatically and keep a copy of every evolution stage.

sections.heading: Auto-evolve
paragraphs: Find the controls in Catch. Auto-evolve is normally on. Turn it off to keep ready Pokémon in their current species until you press Evolve in the PC. Use PC → Ready to evolve to find them.

sections.heading: Living dex
paragraphs: Living dex starts off. When enabled, your best copy of each exact species stops evolving automatically so the earlier stage stays in your collection. Extra copies can still evolve. You can manually evolve a protected copy from its PC card whenever you choose. Living dex does not itself stop the Professor from receiving duplicates; use favorites and Never send protections for that.

sections.heading: Use evolution items
paragraphs: Use evolution items starts off and requires Auto-evolve to be on. Enabling it can immediately use eligible items already in your bag, then use later items as they arrive. Party members get priority, followed by higher IVs.

sections.heading: What automatic items skip
paragraphs: Automatic items do not use Linking Cord, evolve special-look or Perfect Pokémon, choose a branching line such as Eevee, override Everstone, or evolve a Living dex protected copy. Day Care Pokémon, fusions, pending hatch reveals and Pokémon offered in trades also wait. Use their Evolution tab when you want to make the choice yourself.

sections.heading: Never send species
paragraphs: The separate Never send → Species list holds up to 60 seen or registered species. It protects all their copies from auto-send and Send duplicates. Manual bulk transfers can still display a warning and ask for confirmation; favorites remain protected from those transfers.

guides.title: Redeem codes and official gifts
guides.summary: Claim reward codes and gifts from the Tallgrass team.

sections.heading: Redeeming a code
paragraphs: Open Settings → Redeem a code. Enter a code supplied by the Tallgrass team through Discord, streams or events, then press Redeem. Each trainer can use a code once. The result message confirms whether it worked.

sections.heading: Official gifts
paragraphs: Gifts from the Tallgrass team arrive as gift cards. A Pokémon received through one can wear an Event ribbon. Read the gift card to see the reward before collecting it.

sections.heading: Finding active codes
paragraphs: Check current official announcements for codes and their conditions. A sample shown in an input field is not a promise that the sample is an active redeemable code.

guides.title: Limited-time events and announcements
guides.summary: Follow event banners for temporary bonuses, special outbreaks and Raid Hours.

sections.heading: The event banner
paragraphs: When a timed event is running, a banner above the game shows its name, active bonus and countdown. Bonuses can change Shiny odds, EXP, money or Raid Egg rewards. Follow the values on the active banner.

sections.heading: Event outbreaks and Raid Hours
paragraphs: Event outbreaks appear under Events → Outbreaks for trainers who can reach the featured island. A Raid Hour can add bonus eggs during its advertised window. Ordinary badge requirements and the activity’s own entry conditions still apply.

sections.heading: Announcements and gifts
paragraphs: Read team announcements for event details and official reward codes. Official gifts arrive as gift cards, and gifted Pokémon can carry an Event ribbon.

sections.heading: Odds events and Day Care eggs (0.54.3)
paragraphs: Shiny and crystal-odds events also apply to eggs laid in Day Care. The update notes do not provide an additional event multiplier; check the current event's displayed odds.

sections.heading: Spooky season and seasonal stamps
paragraphs: Spectral is a permanent seasonal look available from eligible rolls while Spooky season is active, with a countdown chip linking to its Events card. The 0.57.3 build’s default end is 9 November 2026 at 18:00 UTC; the server can override the window. The Spooky 2026 stamp page and Halloween route decorations use the same season. See the Spectral guide for exact rules.

sections.heading: Surprise events (0.57.4)
paragraphs: The Tallgrass team can start surprise events live: Golden Hour, Spotlight outbreaks, route-wide weather, messages from Glo, Candy Rain and Mystery Egg drops. These are team-run events; their timing and active values come from the game.

Golden Hour boosts Shiny odds, EXP and money for everyone. Read the banner for the active multipliers and countdown; hiding the banner does not end the event. Spotlight features outbreaks of one Pokémon on every island, accessible through Events → Outbreaks.
Route-wide weather can include rain, thunderstorms, snow, a blood moon or the aurora. Follow the active event display rather than assuming ordinary island weather or a fixed schedule.

sections.heading: Hatch Rush (0.57.5)
paragraphs: The Tallgrass team can start Hatch Rush live. While active, Day Care produces eggs at 2× or 3× speed and eggs hatch 2× or 3× sooner. Read the active banner for the multiplier and remaining time; the event has no fixed published schedule.

Hatch Rush changes production and hatching speed, not the probability of a rare trait in each egg. Keep using the breeding builder for per-egg odds. A separate live odds event may have its own effect; Hatch Rush alone is not a shiny or Spectral odds multiplier.

guides.title: Comparing Day Care parents
guides.summary: Inspect both parents’ IVs and natures together before deciding which Pokémon to leave in a pen.

sections.heading: The parent comparison
paragraphs: Open Day Care and select a breeding pen. Each parent displays all six IVs beside the other parent’s values. Green means an IV is higher than the corresponding value on the other parent; red means lower. Equal values stay neutral. A value of 31 is marked as maximum.

sections.heading: Nature colors
paragraphs: Stat labels also reflect each parent’s nature: the boosted stat is green and the lowered stat is red. Compare the label color separately from the IV value color; they describe different things.

sections.heading: Open the full card
paragraphs: Right-click a parent to inspect its full Pokémon card, including nature, ability, moves, items and other details. Use the breeding guide for egg eligibility and bonuses; the side-by-side display shows the parents’ own values.

sections.heading: Egg odds events and evolution timing (0.54.3)
paragraphs: Shiny and crystal-odds events also apply to eggs laid in Day Care. Pokémon removed from Day Care wait until their next level to evolve automatically, or can be evolved manually.

guides.title: Cloud saves and device switching
guides.summary: Continue the same adventure on Windows, Mac or the browser, resolve two-save choices and recover a backup.

sections.heading: Continue on another device
paragraphs: Since 0.56.0, game saves sync through your Discord account. Sign in with the same account on each device. On a fresh installation, the login flow can offer your account save before you choose a new starter.

sections.heading: When Tallgrass finds two saves
paragraphs: If both devices already have progress, compare the offered saves before choosing which adventure to continue. The comparison includes Pokédex progress, Pokémon, money, badges and playtime. The other save is retained as an account backup; the two collections are not merged.
If one save is brand new, the game can retain the more developed adventure automatically and notify you.

sections.heading: Play here
paragraphs: Only one device plays an account at once. Play here retrieves the latest account save before continuing on this device and pauses the other session. Catch-up does not grant duplicate progress for time another device was already playing.

sections.heading: Read the cloud icon
paragraphs: The scene’s cloud icon distinguishes saved, saving, offline, waiting for another device, and a pending two-save choice. Point at it for details or click it to open Cloud save.
Offline progress remains on the current device and uploads after the connection returns. Before switching devices, check that saving has finished.

sections.heading: Save now and restore a backup
paragraphs: Open Settings → Help → Cloud save to save immediately or select an older account copy. Account backups include recent copies, daily copies for a week and saves set aside during a choice. The current adventure is backed up before a restore.

Restoring an older save does not recover ownership of Pokémon already traded, Wonder Traded or sold: they remain with their new trainers. Existing on-device backups and the browser’s Export / Import controls are still available.

sections.heading: Update to 0.56.1
paragraphs: The official 0.56.1 notes report a fix for the 0.56.0 freeze after closing the welcome-back card, plus faster catch-up for large collections.

sections.heading: Phone browser and home-screen app (0.57.0)
paragraphs: iPhone and Android use the same Discord cloud save as the desktop game. The installed iPhone web app uses a short login code and browser hand-off; if automatic login fails, enter that code at play.playtallgrass.com/link in Safari. See Playing on a phone for the full setup.

sections.heading: No cloud save yet (0.57.3)
paragraphs: No cloud save on this account yet means the browser has not received an account copy. Open your existing PC adventure online in 0.56.1 or newer once, using the same Discord account. The browser can then offer that save automatically. Import a save file and Start a new game remain explicit alternatives; creating a new adventure is not required to transfer the old one.

sections.heading: Browser takeover fix (0.57.4)
paragraphs: If Moving your game here waits for another tab that is asleep or closed, the new tab takes over after a few seconds. The old tab cannot overwrite the game afterward.

guides.title: Playing on a phone and installing the web app
guides.summary: Use your Discord cloud save on iPhone or Android, learn touch controls and install Tallgrass on your home screen.

sections.heading: Open the official game
paragraphs: Visit https://play.playtallgrass.com/ in your phone browser and sign in with the same Discord account as your other devices. Version 0.57.0 adds the official phone layout. Review any cloud-save choice before starting a new adventure; Play here moves the active session to this device.

sections.heading: Phone navigation
paragraphs: The hunt stays at the top. Bottom navigation provides Hunt, Party, Events, Day Care and More for the remaining screens. Rotate the phone for a wider view. Islands, Research, Catch, Trainer, Day Care and Settings use smaller groups of tabs.
Friends, trades, offers, Night Market and Glimmer Shop use full-screen phone panels with a close button. Pop-ups adapt to portrait and landscape.

sections.heading: Moving Pokémon by touch
paragraphs: Tap a Pokémon to pick it up, then tap its destination: a PC box, party slot, Day Care pen, Raid squad, trade or Showcase. Tap the selected Pokémon again to cancel.
Press and hold a Pokémon for Move, Card and Info. Tap an icon to read its meaning. Swipe left or right to change pages; in the Pokédex, swipes also navigate between Pokémon.

sections.heading: Battles, Raids and shopping
paragraphs: Phone battles use full-screen controls and large move buttons coloured by type. Tap the battle text to view the log; hold a move to read its details. Tap your Raid squad to edit it.
In the Poké Mart, tap an item, choose ×1, ×5, ×10 or Max, then use Buy. Check the quantity and cost before buying.

sections.heading: Add Tallgrass to your home screen
paragraphs: On iPhone, use Share → Add to Home Screen. On Android, use the browser’s Install option. Settings → This browser → Install provides instructions. Launching the installed web app opens Tallgrass full screen with its own icon.

sections.heading: iPhone home-screen login code
paragraphs: Log in in the iPhone home-screen app displays a short code and opens Discord login. After completing login there, the app should sign in automatically. If it does not, open https://play.playtallgrass.com/link in Safari and enter the displayed code.

sections.heading: Switching away and saving
paragraphs: The 0.57.0 phone rules keep hunting at full speed for the first 2 hours after you switch to another app, then use the normal away pace. Switching away also uploads the save to your account. This is the game’s catch-up rule; it does not require the phone browser to remain visibly running.
Before moving to another device, check the cloud status. One Discord account has one active play session at a time.

sections.heading: If a window or hatch screen stops responding
paragraphs: Update to 0.57.0 before troubleshooting older interface issues. Its release notes report fixes for overlapping welcome/update/hatch screens, egg-count mismatches and trade buttons falling outside short windows. These are documented fixes, rather than a guarantee that every device-specific issue is resolved.

sections.heading: Phone fixes through 0.57.3
paragraphs: The route background is restored when returning to the app. Hearth and Nanny pickers, Raid invite pages, Slots and the New Game Choose button fit their screens. After a freeze the game repairs blocked/click-through input instead of leaving starter selection unusable.

guides.title: Spectral Pokémon and Spooky season
guides.summary: Find permanent ghostly looks during Spooky season, stack rare traits and breed Spectral babies.

sections.heading: When Spectrals are available
paragraphs: The 0.57.4 build defines Spooky season from 26 October 2026 at 18:00 UTC until 9 November 2026 at 18:00 UTC. The server can override these dates; the in-game event countdown is authoritative. New Spectral rolls require the active season and an eligible server-issued roll. A fallback offline/local roll does not produce a new Spectral.

Once obtained, a Spectral keeps the look after the season ends. From 0.57.4, Spectrals also have Ghostly: a 10% chance to dodge attacks outside Raids. Their card displays the effect; it does not apply in Raids.

sections.heading: Where they come from
paragraphs: Eligible wild encounters, ordinary starters, Day Care, gift and Costume Eggs, Raid Eggs and Tower Pokémon can be Spectral. It can coexist with Shiny, Void, Prismatic, Alpha, Perfect and a costume where the source supports those traits. Founder rewards retain their fixed traits.

sections.heading: Exact odds before live odds events
paragraphs: Spectral chance is 80% of the source’s Prismatic base chance: multiply that probability by 0.8, or multiply its denominator by 1.25. Rank, Charm and the successful Radar chain therefore affect ordinary wild Spectral odds. Live Shiny/crystal event multipliers also apply where supported. The calculator excludes these live multipliers.

sections.heading: Day Care parents
paragraphs: Use the Day Care Prismatic base after rank, Charm and any different-origin-island bonus, multiply it by 0.8, then add 1 in 1,280 for each Spectral parent. The Spectral-parent bonus is separate from the Prismatic-parent bonus: a Prismatic parent alone does not add a Spectral-parent bonus. The season must still be active. Two Spectral parents add 1 in 640 in total, plus the base chance.
Changing parents does not reroll the traits of eggs already laid. Use the breeding builder to include species compatibility, costumes and all other traits.

sections.heading: Finding, catching and trading
paragraphs: Search spectral or spooky in the PC, use the Spectral Show filter, or use the Pokédex Spectral filter. Trainer statistics count Spectral finds. Catch includes Spectral and Never send → Spectral, both enabled initially; Master Ball rules can also select Spectral.
Spectrals use the rare trade category shared with Void and Prismatic. They can be listed on the Night Market and add 50 Glimmer to a find’s value before any applicable rarity multiplier.

sections.heading: Seasonal stamps and route decorations
paragraphs: Events → Stamps has the separate Spooky 2026 challenge page. Existing self-found Spectrals count; trades do not. Complete all six seasonal challenges before the season ends for the Spooky 2026 card frame and title. Seasonal stamps do not add to the ordinary book totals.
Routes gain Halloween scenery during the event. The lanterns, webs, candles, bats and sky are background decorations and disappear when the season ends.

sections.heading: Ghostly in battle (0.57.4)
paragraphs: Spectral Pokémon have a 10% chance to dodge attacks outside Raids. Look for Ghostly on their card. The Spectral Evolution row now marks only the forms you have registered as Spectral.

guides.title: Costume combinations and breeding odds
guides.summary: Costumes can combine with rare traits, but their chance depends on where the Pokémon comes from.

sections.heading: Costume is a separate condition
paragraphs: A costume is not a universal sixth rarity roll. A Costume Egg or a named costume prize already has its costume. Wild costumes depend on an active costume outbreak or a guest encounter. Day Care passes down only eligible Halloween costumes during its inheritance event. Calculate the other traits using the selected source’s odds.

Use gift or Raid Egg trait odds; a specifically named Costume Egg is a different source.

sections.heading: Halloween inheritance dates
paragraphs: In version 0.54.0, Halloween costume inheritance runs until November 1, 2026 at 00:00 UTC. Eggs created before the cutoff retain their costume when hatched later. After the cutoff, the same pair no longer adds an inherited Halloween costume to newly created eggs.

sections.heading: Which babies inherit it
paragraphs: The baby must belong to the costume’s matching family. With Ditto and an eligible costume parent, the baby follows the non-Ditto family and receives the costume. A same-family compatible pair with an eligible costume also gives costume babies. With two different non-Ditto families, either parent family can be selected; a costume belonging only to one family does not dress a baby from the other family.
bullets: Ditto + matching Halloween costume parent: costume is guaranteed while inheritance is active.
Same-family pair with matching Halloween costume: costume is guaranteed while inheritance is active.
Two different families, only one with an eligible Halloween costume: half the babies follow that costume family, provided the pair is compatible.
Two eligible Halloween costume families: whichever family is selected has its matching costume.
Non-Halloween costumes do not pass down through this Halloween inheritance rule.

sections.heading: Can one Pokémon have all six traits?
paragraphs: Yes, the Day Care can produce a Costume Pokémon that is Shiny, Void, Prismatic, Alpha and Perfect together. Use a compatible pair that supplies a matching Halloween costume and at least one Alpha parent. A same-family pair keeps the costume part guaranteed while the event is active; the other five traits still need to succeed.

For example, Ghost-sheet Charmander and an Alpha Charizard are the same family. Their babies are Charmander with the matching Halloween costume during the event. The Alpha parent adds a 1-in-64 Alpha chance; each other trait follows the usual breeding formula.

sections.heading: Calculating the combined chance
paragraphs: For an eligible guaranteed-costume baby, the chance of all six together is shiny chance × Void chance × Prismatic chance × Perfect chance × Alpha chance. If only half the pair’s babies belong to the costume family, multiply by ½. A request for an exact look also multiplies by the failure probability of every rare trait you want absent.
This is a chance per eligible egg. It does not include the time to obtain compatible parents, find a costume prize or open the relevant content.

sections.heading: Wild guest chances
paragraphs: On an island with an active outbreak, after an encounter misses the 12% outbreak replacement, the guest check is 1 in 400. That is not a global costume rate for every wild encounter: Radar and outbreak conditions must be satisfied, the current guest must exist, and a costume outbreak has its own separate 12% target path.
Once the game has selected a costume encounter, calculate its rare-look combination with that encounter’s own odds. Do not multiply by an invented universal costume percentage.

sections.heading: Tower and costumes
paragraphs: Tower wild recruits have no generated costume. The Climb starter keeps its existing Shiny, Void, Prismatic and Alpha traits, but the run’s starter copy does not carry its costume. This does not remove the costume from your original Pokémon in the PC.

sections.heading: Add Spectral for all seven traits
paragraphs: A compatible Day Care pair can also add Spectral during the active season, giving seven traits including Costume. Multiply the six-trait probability above by the pair’s Spectral chance. The costume inheritance window and Spectral season are separate: both must permit the new egg. Spectral parents alone do not extend either window.

The builder lists 128 exact patterns and 16 Shiny/Void/Prismatic/Spectral sprite previews. The older six-trait calculations above leave Spectral unspecified. Use Required or Excluded to include it in an exact result.

guides.title: Game Corner
guides.summary: Capsules, Slots, cosmetic prizes and the Coin exchange in one place.

sections.heading: Choose your activity
paragraphs: Open Events, then Game Corner. Capsule Machine offers collectible cosmetics, Slots spends Coins for a chance at a payout, and the Prize Counter lets you choose a specific capsule cosmetic.
bullets: Capsule Machine: single pulls, ten pulls, daily free pull and rarity guarantees.
Slots: Coin bets, winning lines and payouts.
Prize Counter: trade Coins for a chosen cosmetic or a Capsule Token.
Coin exchange: buy 100 Coins for $5,000.

sections.heading: Plan your collection
paragraphs: Use the separate activity guides for exact prices, drop rates, duplicate refunds and limits. The cosmetics catalog lists all 301 Style entries, including capsule rarities and available shop prices.

guides.title: Coin exchange
guides.summary: Turn game money into Game Corner Coins.

sections.heading: Exchange rate
paragraphs: At the Game Corner, $5,000 buys 100 Coins. Coins also come from Slots payouts and duplicate capsule rewards.

sections.heading: What Coins buy
paragraphs: The Prize Counter sells capsule cosmetics for 600 / 1,800 / 6,000 / 24,000 Coins at Common / Rare / Epic / Legendary rarity. One Capsule Token costs 1,000 Coins and pays for one single capsule pull.

guides.title: About this fan-made wiki
guides.summary: An unofficial player companion for Tallgrass version 0.57.3.

sections.heading: Made for your next hunt
paragraphs: Tallgrass — Fan-Made Wiki is an unofficial reference for ordinary play: building squads, catching Pokémon, breeding, events, progression and collecting. It is not affiliated with the game’s developers.

sections.heading: Version and coverage
paragraphs: This edition covers version 0.57.3. Updates can change prices, balance, rewards and requirements. Pokémon pages include alternate forms and costumes where available; a catalog entry does not mean a Pokémon is obtainable as an ordinary wild encounter. Check its listed encounter locations and the relevant feature guide.

sections.heading: Reading the reference
paragraphs: Odds describe an eligible roll, not a guarantee after a set number of encounters. Ordinary starters, Founder rewards, wild encounters, Day Care, Tower and Raid Eggs use different rules. Ordinary ability descriptions are separate from the 40 signature squad Leader skills.

guides.title: Wild Dex and self-found badges
guides.summary: Track Pokémon you caught or hatched yourself and earn Bronze through Master badges.

sections.heading: Your own catches and breeding lines
paragraphs: Wild Dex is a separate collection goal beside the Pokédex. It tracks species you catch or hatch yourself, together with their evolved forms. Ordinary Pokédex registration and Trainer rank remain separate systems.

Trades, Wonder Trades, Night Market purchases and gifts do not qualify. A baby also fails to qualify if any of those sources appears in its family. Breed from your own eligible Pokémon to grow the collection.

sections.heading: What carries over
paragraphs: Qualifying catches from before 0.57.5 count. Eggs hatched before the update do not count toward Wild Dex because they have no family record. This does not remove their ordinary Pokédex registration.

guides.title: Hatch Rush and faster Day Care eggs
guides.summary: A live event speeds up egg production and hatching without changing per-egg odds.

sections.heading: A live surprise event
paragraphs: The Tallgrass team can start Hatch Rush live. While active, Day Care produces eggs at 2× or 3× speed and eggs hatch 2× or 3× sooner. Read the active banner for the multiplier and remaining time; the event has no fixed published schedule.

sections.heading: More attempts, unchanged odds
paragraphs: Hatch Rush changes production and hatching speed, not the probability of a rare trait in each egg. Keep using the breeding builder for per-egg odds. A separate live odds event may have its own effect; Hatch Rush alone is not a shiny or Spectral odds multiplier.

sections.heading: Where to check it
paragraphs: A golden egg banner shows the countdown, and Day Care displays the event near the Egg Basket. Hiding its banner does not stop Hatch Rush. Keep compatible pens supplied and clear basket space so faster production can continue.

guides.title: What’s new in Tallgrass 0.57.5
guides.summary: Wild Dex, Bug Hunter badges, a fifth pen, Auto-favourite, Hatch Rush and new Night Market rules.

sections.heading: 0.57.5: Wild Dex and Bug Hunter badges
paragraphs: Wild Dex is a separate collection goal beside the Pokédex. It tracks species you catch or hatch yourself, together with their evolved forms. Ordinary Pokédex registration and Trainer rank remain separate systems.

Trades, Wonder Trades, Night Market purchases and gifts do not qualify. A baby also fails to qualify if any of those sources appears in its family. Breed from your own eligible Pokémon to grow the collection.
Qualifying catches from before 0.57.5 count. Eggs hatched before the update do not count toward Wild Dex because they have no family record. This does not remove their ordinary Pokédex registration.
Wild Dex badges require 100 / 300 / 600 / 900 qualifying species for Bronze / Silver / Gold / Master. Each bug confirmed by the Tallgrass team adds a Bug Hunter badge to your profile.

sections.heading: Fifth pen, Auto-favourite and Hatch Rush
paragraphs: Buy the fifth pen in the Glimmer Shop after completing every island or reaching Professor rank. It adds another breeding pair; the earlier four pen unlocks remain.

Settings → Auto-favourite lets you select Shiny, Void, Prismatic, Spectral, Perfect and Legendary. New catches and hatches matching selected categories receive a favourite star. Existing Pokémon stay as they are. Favourites are protected from auto-send, Send duplicates, the Professor and Wonder Trade.

The Tallgrass team can start Hatch Rush live. While active, Day Care produces eggs at 2× or 3× speed and eggs hatch 2× or 3× sooner. Read the active banner for the multiplier and remaining time; the event has no fixed published schedule.

Hatch Rush changes production and hatching speed, not the probability of a rare trait in each egg. Keep using the breeding builder for per-egg odds. A separate live odds event may have its own effect; Hatch Rush alone is not a shiny or Spectral odds multiplier.

sections.heading: Night Market rules
paragraphs: The price picker begins at the current minimum and displays it. Perfect, Alpha and Legendary status can raise the minimum; combinations use the applicable higher price rather than simply adding the base values.

Examples from this release: Shiny Alpha 300, Prismatic Alpha 2,250 and Void Legendary 800 Glimmer. Earlier evolution stages add 10% for the first stage and 5% for the middle stage of a three-stage line, or 5% for the first stage of a two-stage line. A Shiny Charmander therefore starts at 110 Glimmer. Check the picker for the exact combined minimum.

Shiny purchases unlock from island 5, Void from island 7, and Prismatic and Spectral after every island is complete. Locked stalls show the required island. The market itself still opens with the third Gym badge.

Each player may make one Spectral listing per UTC day, resetting at midnight UTC. Listings below the new minimum prices returned to their sellers’ PCs with a Hunt log note; they can be listed again at a valid price.
Only N in the world now counts Spectral-only looks too and refreshes every few minutes. The minimum listing price is different from the Glimmer reward for finding a Pokémon.

rows: Legendary or Mythical without a special look

sections.heading: Tower and Raid repairs
paragraphs: Runs upload as soon as they end. The end screen reports Saving, Run saved to the board or a retry state. Failed uploads retry automatically, including after restart; click the status to retry immediately.

Runs ending with five or six Pokémon now upload with the whole party. Missing personal-best and weekly-best records upload automatically on this version. Each friends board shows its top 50 in pages that fit the window, and keeps your own row and place visible. Desktop empty-row and phone layout problems are fixed.
Friends with no passes left today appear in a No passes today group and cannot be invited; eligible friends are listed first.

Party members who only watch no longer inflate boss HP. A member who skips their first round removes their share of boss HP, but can still join in and attack later. The defeat card now fits the smallest phones.

sections.heading: Cards, player tags and themes
paragraphs: Pokémon cards display how many of that kind exist worldwide for Shiny, Void, Prismatic and Spectral looks, including their combinations. These counts describe existing Pokémon, not the chance of finding one.
A small grey friend-code suffix distinguishes players with the same name on boards, Raid screens, the Night Market, Friends’ finds and friend cards. Hover to see the full code.
The Pokédex theme uses a black shell, gold crowns and trim, a blue lens and three lights. The active tab has a crown. Both it and Game Boy now style window frames, title bars, tabs and the strip bar.

Game Boy keeps its four-green palette for scenery and interface, while Pokémon retain their real colours so rare looks remain distinguishable. Text is clearer and Shop previews show other themes in their own colours.

sections.heading: 0.57.4: live surprise events
paragraphs: The Tallgrass team can start surprise events live: Golden Hour, Spotlight outbreaks, route-wide weather, messages from Glo, Candy Rain and Mystery Egg drops. These are team-run events; their timing and active values come from the game.

Golden Hour boosts Shiny odds, EXP and money for everyone. Read the banner for the active multipliers and countdown; hiding the banner does not end the event. Spotlight features outbreaks of one Pokémon on every island, accessible through Events → Outbreaks.
Route-wide weather can include rain, thunderstorms, snow, a blood moon or the aurora. Follow the active event display rather than assuming ordinary island weather or a fixed schedule.

sections.heading: Spectral Ghostly and seasonal stamps
paragraphs: Spectral Pokémon gain a 10% chance to dodge attacks outside Raids, shown as Ghostly on their card. Spirit Collector now requires 25 Spectrals instead of 50 and completes automatically if you already qualify. The Evolution row correctly marks forms registered as Spectral.

sections.heading: Raid preparation and Cheer all
paragraphs: Each Pokémon in the Raid squad shows its held item. A glowing recommendation identifies a better item in your Bag for the current boss; hover for the reason and use Equip all to apply the recommendations.

Suggested squad tests candidates against the exact boss, tries type pairs for Synergies and selects suitable held items from your Bag. The update retains the previous suggestion as a minimum; if the stronger choice depends on items, Equip all brings in that squad with its items. Spectral Ghostly dodge does not apply in Raids.
Friends’ finds → Cheer all cheers every find you have not cheered yet, then reports the friendship points earned. The cap remains 3 cheer points per day with each friend.

sections.heading: Battle fixes
paragraphs: Focus Sash now leaves the holder at 1 HP when the hit lands and lets it make its move. Stamina triggers from confusion self-damage. Fused Necrozma, Kyurem and Calyrex retain their fused forms in friend battles.

sections.heading: Browser, display and interface repairs
paragraphs: Browser device switching recovers when another tab is asleep or closed, while preventing the old tab from overwriting the game. New Game accepts clicks after Discord login. Use all monitors remains enabled after updates or restarts, and the Game Boy theme slowdown is fixed.

Large gift batches fit on screen and the reward card closes with X or Esc. The Raid defeat card X works on phones. Friends’ online counts support lists above 1,000, and idle online checks use less data.

sections.heading: 0.57.3: friendship and Raids
paragraphs: Friendship now counts opened gifts, trades, shared Raid wins, rare-find cheers and friend battles. Previous activity counts, while the existing days and 3 / 10 / 20 point thresholds remain. Hearts show progress and today’s actions. Cheers grant both friends points within the daily cap.

Two Raid bosses appear per UTC day, at midnight and noon: Mythical first, then Legendary or Ultra Beast. The card previews the next boss; existing fights have a 30-minute grace period. Received Pokémon now wait 30 days before re-trading.

sections.heading: Spooky 2026 and Spectral
paragraphs: The seasonal Spectral look stacks with other traits, remains after the event and can arise in wild encounters, starters, eggs, Raids and the Tower. Day Care has Spectral-parent additions. Search, Catch, Never send, Master Ball rules, stats and the Night Market support it.

A separate six-challenge stamp page awards a frame and title. Previous self-found Spectrals count, trades do not, and seasonal stamps do not contribute to normal totals. Every route gains temporary Halloween decorations. Builders now support Spectral and the calculator lists 128 exact trait patterns.

sections.heading: Clearer cards, slots and eggs
paragraphs: Mythical and Ultra Beast have distinct labels and searchable filters; broad legendary searches still include them. Card Pixel / HD is remembered, card HD respects its own setting, and rare finds record their Radar chain and discovery odds.

Lucky Slots highlights only the paying middle line, counts Cherries from the left, explains payouts and shows pay-table amounts for the bet. Coins update when reels stop, Auto ×10 keeps its bet, and phones have a pay-table button. Egg totals count the same ready eggs across the hunt, basket and reveal, with warming eggs explained.

sections.heading: Repairs through 0.57.3
paragraphs: Fixes cover fused Kyurem/Necrozma/Calyrex disappearing after saving, gift-claim feedback and cross-device counters, unrevealed babies being auto-sent, cut-off Hearth/Nanny pickers, Evolution-row alignment, missing cries, phone backgrounds on return, and hunt timing.

Earlier hotfixes repair walking without encounters, slow-roll waiting, input after freezes, the cut-off New Game Choose button, interrupted gate loading, hidden Inbox gifts, duplicate friends, Raid invite pagination, fainted Tower vitamins and rest timers stuck for hours. Rush now explains stops and upcoming bosses.

sections.heading: Cloud saves and paused sessions
paragraphs: An inactive device dims and shows Paused with Play here. When the browser has no cloud save, it explains how to upload an existing PC adventure by opening 0.56.1 or newer online, offers import or a fresh game, and automatically offers the account save when it arrives.

sections.heading: Verified current odds change
paragraphs: The 0.57.3 installed outbreak tuning is Looks ×1, replacing the older ×3. Radar still reaches ×3 at chain 200. The calculator and current guides use the installed value; live server event multipliers are separate.

sections.heading: 0.57.0: phone play and touch controls
paragraphs: Play the official site on iPhone or Android with your Discord cloud save. The hunt is at the top with bottom tabs, portrait and landscape panels, tap-to-move Pokémon, hold menus, icon explanations and swipe navigation. Phone battles have large type-coloured buttons and touch access to move details and the log.

Raids support tap-to-edit squads, the Pokédex supports swipes, and the Mart has quantity choices and a large Buy button. Friends, trade offers, Night Market and Glimmer Shop open full screen; other phone screens group their controls into tabs.

sections.heading: Install and log in on iPhone or Android
paragraphs: Add the game to the iPhone home screen through Share, or use Install on Android. Settings → This browser → Install explains the steps. The iPhone installed app uses a short Discord login code, with play.playtallgrass.com/link in Safari as a fallback.
After switching away on a phone, hunting keeps full speed for 2 hours before using away pace. The save uploads when switching away. The browser’s welcome text now explains the shared cloud save.

sections.heading: Rare-find sharing and catch protections
paragraphs: Settings has a separate Show my rare finds in the Discord switch for posting especially rare finds with your trainer name. Catch → Never send has a Costume option enabled by default.
Send duplicates and auto-send exclude Event Pokémon and locked-box Pokémon. PC Send also excludes Event Pokémon. Catch everything bypasses the Catch list’s minimum IVs.

sections.heading: Breeding, items and rare-look clarity
paragraphs: Day Care eggs keep the nature assigned when laid; later parent changes do not alter eggs already in the basket. Everstone and Destiny Knot application fixes cover every eligible egg. Destiny Knot uses the best of three new IV rolls and copies no parent IVs.
Luck Incense and Prism Aura descriptions now say extra copies do not stack. Radar and outbreaks label their Shiny, Void and Prismatic multiplier as Looks.

sections.heading: Trading, cards and update controls
paragraphs: The release fixes trade and sale eligibility for online catches and Day Care babies, including Wonder Trade for babies. Existing feature requirements still apply. Trade cards shrink in short windows so confirmation and offer buttons stay visible.

Card shortcuts to the Shop, Lab and Buddy close the card; Esc cancels renaming. The Bag and windows opened by a card appear above it. Settings → Help shows the version on Patch notes and offers a PC Updates tile to check and restart.

sections.heading: Hatching and battle fixes
paragraphs: Welcome, away-summary, update-note and hatch screens open in sequence. Egg counts agree across All, Open all and reveal, and newly ready eggs join an ongoing reveal.

Move details stay inside the battle text box without making buttons jump. Fake Out and First Impression are limited to the Pokémon’s first turn out in automatic and manual battles. Wild transformed Ditto shows its copied appearance while keeping its name. Necrozma, Kyurem and Calyrex fusions use fused walking sprites.

sections.heading: 0.56.1: welcome-back freeze fix
paragraphs: The release fixes the freeze reported after closing the welcome-back card in 0.56.0. It also speeds up catch-up for saves containing thousands of Pokémon.

sections.heading: 0.56.0: one adventure across devices
paragraphs: Discord cloud saves let you continue the same adventure on Windows, Mac or the official browser game. A fresh install can offer your existing account save; two developed saves can be compared before choosing which to continue.

sections.heading: Account backups and the cloud icon
paragraphs: The scene’s cloud icon reports sync status. Settings → Help → Cloud save provides immediate saving and older account copies. A restore keeps a backup of the current save and does not duplicate Pokémon already traded or sold.

sections.heading: Classic fullscreen
paragraphs: Use F11 to expand Classic; F11 or Esc restores its earlier size.

sections.heading: New in 0.55.0
paragraphs: Only one device can play an account at a time. Press Play on the device you want to use; the other device pauses. Catch-up counts only time when no other device was playing.

Stone Axe is a Move Tutor move Kleavor can learn. A successful hit leaves pointed stones that hurt each Pokémon entering the opposing side. Ursaluna can learn Blood Moon from the Move Tutor; it cannot be used on consecutive turns.

sections.heading: Battle and raid updates in 0.55.0
paragraphs: Raid invitations now list only friends with five Gym badges, and show how many friends are not eligible yet. Tower evolution choices include the evolved form’s level 1 and earlier-level moves. Wo-Chien, Chien-Pao, Ting-Lu and Chi-Yu explain their Ruin ability when they enter.

In harsh sunlight or Electric Terrain, Protosynthesis and Quark Drive boost the user’s highest stat: Speed by 50%, other stats by 30%. The boost is reported in battle and ends with the weather or terrain. These abilities do not apply in raids.

sections.heading: Odds and collecting in 0.55.0
paragraphs: The Shiny, Void and Prismatic odds display includes the active event multiplier. Use the shown rate for the current eligible roll.

sections.heading: New in 0.54.5
paragraphs: Show on Discord can display your island, Tower floor or raid, and briefly show a Shiny, Void, Prismatic or Legendary catch. The Discord app must be open; turn the feature off in Settings → Show on Discord.
Shiny and crystal odds events also boost rare looks on Tower Route and Den floors. The daily friend gift opening limit increased from 10 to 20.

sections.heading: Changes in 0.54.5
paragraphs: Self-Destruct and Explosion faint their user unless Damp prevents it; in raids, their user is out for the rest of that raid. Updates give a restart countdown, with required updates able to restart while you are away. Rush shows its charges and next recharge.

Day Care parents show their natures, and the help panel explains Ditto, Destiny Knot, Everstone and trait inheritance. Alpha boss notices explain recruitment by defeating them; Alpha bosses cannot be caught with balls. The Night Market explains how long a new account must wait before selling.

Raid parties have a direct Leave party button, timed invitations and a searchable invite list. Trainers with tied scores keep a consistent order and your row remains visible outside the top 100. Favourites must be unstarred before trading or listing them.

sections.heading: Fixes in 0.54.5
paragraphs: This release fixed duplicate Professor sends involving favourites, improved the login card’s account-switch and sign-out choices, made friend battles use the team present when the battle runs, corrected raid pass counts, and fixed the Join the Discord link.

sections.heading: Earlier additions in 0.54.0–0.54.4
paragraphs: Mega Evolution details, terrain effects, Ditto’s Transform, new PC filters and catch rules, more breeding pens and IV comparison, the Pokédex Skills book, Everstone nature inheritance, and added duplicate-send protections arrived in the preceding updates. See their individual guides for details.

odds.title: Tallgrass rare-look odds

probabilityMeaning.marginal: The named trait, whether or not other looks also appear.
probabilityMeaning.exactLooks: Exactly the named Shiny/Void/Prismatic combination; does not restrict Perfect or Alpha.
probabilityMeaning.inclusiveLooks: All named looks, while allowing additional looks.
probabilityMeaning.perfect: The dedicated Perfect bonus roll. Natural IV spreads without that bonus are not included.
probabilityMeaning.alpha: Alpha trait roll, where this source has one.
probabilityMeaning.jointTraits: For independent sources, multiply the required trait probabilities and the failure probabilities for traits you explicitly exclude. Leave unrestricted traits out.
probabilityMeaning.all64Combinations: Exact requirements and exclusions across six traits. For independent trait sources multiply each required probability and each excluded failure probability; apply costume only from its source/family condition. Tower rare looks are mutually exclusive.

ordinaryStarter.label: Ordinary new-game starter
notes: All 27 ordinary starter choices use these same odds.
Starter looks roll separately, so combinations are possible.
There is no dedicated Perfect bonus roll or Alpha roll for the ordinary starter.

founderStarter.label: Founder thank-you starter
notes: A separate once-only Founder reward: Prismatic with perfect IVs.
It does not use the ordinary starter odds.

modifiers.label: Outbreak target
modifiers.formula: Multiply rare-look probabilities by the current outbreak tuning: ×1 in 0.57.3.
modifiers.details: After an eligible Radar encounter is ruled out, the active outbreak replaces an ordinary encounter 12% of the time.

modifiers.label: Radar target
modifiers.formula: Multiply all three rare-look probabilities by 1 + min(chain, 200) / 100.
modifiers.details: Unlocks with badge 6. Registered non-legendary target chance 30%; seen but unregistered target 10%; an eligible registered legendary target 5%. A charge provides 25 target encounters. The chain increments on a target encounter before its odds are calculated.

modifiers.label: Day Care base
modifiers.formula: Ordinary wild rare-look probabilities × 1.5; base Perfect chance stays the rank’s Perfect chance.

modifiers.label: Parents caught on different islands
modifiers.formula: Double the base rare-look part before adding parent bonuses.

modifiers.label: Rare-look parents
modifiers.formula: Shiny = base + shiny parent count / 128; Void = base + Void parent count / 384; Prismatic = base + Prismatic parent count / 1024.

modifiers.label: Perfect parents
modifiers.formula: Perfect chance = rank Perfect chance + Perfect parent count / 48.

modifiers.label: Destiny Knot on a parent
modifiers.formula: Perfect chance = min(1, (rank Perfect chance + Perfect parent count / 48) × 3).
modifiers.stacking: One and two Destiny Knots have the same effect.
modifiers.details: Also keeps the best total IV spread of three rolls for a non-Perfect baby; does not add inherited parent IVs.

modifiers.label: Costume Egg reward
modifiers.formula: Ordinary wild rare-look probabilities × 3; Perfect chance 1/100.
modifiers.details: Used for Costume Egg rewards, including qualifying Tower milestones and costume rewards. It differs from a prize costume encounter.

modifiers.label: Ordinary gift egg
modifiers.formula: Ordinary wild rare-look probabilities × 1.5; no dedicated Perfect or Alpha bonus roll.

modifiers.label: Prize costume encounter
modifiers.formula: Uses ordinary rank and Charm rare-look chances and rank Perfect chance.
modifiers.details: A costume granted as a prize encounter does not automatically receive the Costume Egg ×3 bonus.

modifiers.label: Tower Luck
modifiers.formula: L = min(14, shiny count + 2 × Void count + 3 × Prismatic count + Alpha count + 2 × Shiny Charm reward count); multiplier = 1 + L / 4.
modifiers.details: Tower Shiny Charm rewards are separate from the Mart upgrade. Ordered rare-look checks: Prismatic below multiplier/6000; otherwise Void below multiplier/1800; otherwise Shiny below multiplier/300.

modifiers.label: Tower Den
modifiers.semantics: Mutually exclusive looks, not three independent rolls.

notes: Parent additions are additive probability, not denominator reductions.
Different-island bonus applies only to the base look portion.
Destiny Knot does not improve shiny, Void, Prismatic or Alpha odds.
Hearth, Fire types and Nanny change timing, not odds per egg.
Joined bosses have no Shiny, Void or Prismatic look roll.
Alpha status comes from the boss type; it is not an ordinary wild-encounter percentage.
These are join chances after victory, not chances to encounter a boss.
Catching probability is separate from the chance of finding a rare look.
Master Balls always catch.
Outside Tower, a critical catch independently succeeds with 1% + 0.5% per badge, up to 5%.
A successful catch preserves the Pokémon’s rare looks.
